en.title: iPhone Duo orders limited to two per customer as Apple tackles scalping
en.summary: Apple is limiting iPhone Duo orders to a maximum of two per customer in the US, UK, and elsewhere after shipping dates slipped into January of next year within minutes of pre-orders opening . The move appears to be an attempt to tackle the problem of scalping, where people buy large volumes of supply-constrained devices in order to resell them on eBay for well above the retail price … more…
en.body:
Apple is limiting iPhone Duo orders to a maximum of two per customer in the US, UK, and elsewhere after shipping dates slipped into January of next year within minutes of pre-orders opening .

The move appears to be an attempt to tackle the problem of scalping, where people buy large volumes of supply-constrained devices in order to resell them on eBay for well above the retail price …

Engadget reports that it tried to add more than two iPhone Duo units to its cart on the Apple stores in the US, UK, Japan, and Spain, and received a notification advising it of the limit.

We’ve tried adding more than two units to our cart on the Apple Stores for Japan, Spain and the United Kingdom, in addition to the US, and we’ve received a warning notice across all the online stores. The notification said: “A maximum of 2 iPhone Duo can be purchased per customer. Please adjust the total quantity of iPhone Duo in your order before checking out.”

The site said that the same limit applies no matter what configuration you select.

The company is almost certainly implementing the move in a bid to reduce scalping. We’ve already seen dozens of iPhone Duos listed on eBay by scalpers, some with prices exceeding $5,000 .

It’s not the first time Apple has imposed limits on supply-constrained iPhones. The company has done this in China multiple times, with limits applied to walk-in purchases in retail stores as well as those made online. The company has also done it in the US before , with the first example being the iPhone 5 way back in 2012.

Industrial-level scalping is hard to defeat. Organized gangs use multiple virtual credit card numbers, email addresses, and delivery addresses in order to circumvent limits. Others pay people to place orders on their behalf.

All the same, it’s good to see Apple at least attempting to reduce the scale of the problem. It’s also possible the company is implementing other behind-the-scenes measures to detect and reject more sophisticated bulk purchase attempts.

As we predicted , some customers have seen improvements to their estimated delivery dates. It’s also worth trying for a walk-in purchase if you live close to an Apple store – just not on day one .

en.title: Yelp can now call on your behalf to check wait times at a restaurant
en.summary: Yelp is embedding numerous new AI features into its app that can do everything from call to check on restaurant wait times to create personalized recommendations that remember your preferences.
en.body:
Over the last few weeks, personal assistants like Instinct, Fo, and Muse have enabled users to call businesses for customer support and appointment booking. Following this trend, Yelp is adding the ability for its app users to get a voice agent to call a restaurant to check wait times.

The new feature, Check for Me, will show up on restaurant pages in the app, where users can enter their party size and phone number. The AI agent then calls on behalf of the user to check wait times and texts them the results to decide if they want to go to that particular restaurant.

Last year, Yelp debuted its voice solution for restaurants and service providers . With this new feature, the discovery platform is fulfilling the consumer side of the equation, though there is a possibility that a user’s agent will talk to the restaurant’s agent, and agent-to-agent communication might break down the conversation.

The company is also updating its Yelp AI assistant that helps users discover restaurants and services. With the new OpenTable integration, users can easily book a restaurant without leaving the app.

Yelp is adding better personalization to its assistant by having it remember preferences that you might have mentioned in previous chats. Plus, you can access your chat history from the past 30 days in the app, with full history available soon.

Users can ask the chatbot to set custom reminders, such as sending suggestions for weekend activities every Friday. The company is also letting users build their own lists, starting with two “Been Here” and “Want to Go” lists. You can filter your lists by location, category, and cuisine, reorder, add notes to items, and share them with others.

Next month, the company will start showing weekly personalized recommendations based on your saved items and rankings. Yelp is also working on converting collections to lists and giving the lists tab a new look, rolling out later in the year, along with a maps view.

To cap off all these changes, Yelp has been thinking about enhancing customer support and business processes through AI. In the new update, the company is releasing a new paid product called Smart Lead Reply, which can reply to customers and engage with them to qualify a lead. Business owners, who will be charged $30 per month for these services, can specify how an agent should handle a conversation with a customer. Other companies like Meta have also been courting small businesses with AI offerings to handle inbound customer inquiries .

en.title: Otter.ai raises $320 million from General Catalyst’s growth fund for its meeting tool
en.summary: Meeting note-taking tool Otter.ai announced on Tuesday that it has raised $320 million from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF), which provides capital to startups without diluting equity and gets returns on the results of marketing spend. Otter.ai said that it will use these funds for enterprise growth, go-to-market strategy, international expansion, and product innovation. […]
en.body:
Meeting note-taking tool Otter.ai announced on Tuesday that it has raised $320 million from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF), which provides capital to startups without diluting equity and gets returns on the results of marketing spend.

Otter.ai said that it will use these funds for enterprise growth, go-to-market strategy, international expansion, and product innovation.

The startup, which has been around for nearly a decade, has raised $50 million in total funding with its last round in 2021, according to PitchBook data.

Last year, Otter hit a revenue milestone after crossing $100 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR) . The company said it’s now approaching new milestones, but didn’t provide updated figures.

The company said that 40 million users have used its product to date, up from 25 million last year. However, given the crowded space among meeting note-taking products, a pertinent challenge for Otter would be to have its customers stick around. Unfortunately, the startup didn’t provide any numbers around its monthly active users or churn.

“Voice is one of the biggest untapped opportunities in enterprise AI, and Otter is at the forefront of it – a conviction that’s only deepened watching Otter’s growth,” said Pranav Singhvi, Partner and Co-founder of CVF, General Catalyst. “When Otter enables enterprises to capture critical voice data and turns it into actionable business insights, teams move faster, decisions get sharper, and productivity compounds across the organization, and that’s why it’s a strong partner for CVF.”

There is a lot of competition in the market with well-funded meeting notetakers like Fireflies.ai, Granola , and Read AI ; new entrants like Calendly , Wispr , and Superhuman, which acquired Fathom ; and other notetakers like Circleback, Talat, and Quill.

Most of these notetakers want to connect to enterprise systems and, based on data captured in meetings, automate workflows. Otter is also heading in that direction. In the last few years, it introduced a meeting assistant , a search function that works across apps , and integration with other AI tools .

Otter’s newly appointed CMO, Alex Gay, who comes from Superhuman, told TechCrunch at a sit-down at the HumanX conference last month that the company sees a big opportunity in turning transcripts into an actionable roadmap for people who are in back-to-back meetings.

“When we start thinking about what is actually the bigger problem that people are facing right now, we saw this large pain point in meeting-heavy roles, where people are back-to-back in conversations. These meetings are the work for them. That’s either customer conversations or, from a sales standpoint. That’s where strategies are discussed. But meetings are terribly inefficient because when you come into a meeting, you spend the first twenty minutes recapping what was said before to catch everybody up,” he said.

The company is now experimenting with providing insights before, after, and during meetings. It has been testing a feature to send a pre-brief to users with details and background information, with context from previous conversations across surfaces. Plus, it is also trying out a Live Assist feature to let users ask questions to the AI assistant during the meeting to get knowledge.

en.title: The Apple Store will only let you check out two iPhone Duos
en.summary: Apple is limiting iPhone Duo purchases to two per customers around the world.
en.body:
Apple will warn you to adjust the number of Duos in your cart if you attempt to buy more than two.

Apple is limiting the number of iPhone Duo units you can pre-order to two per customer, not just in the US, but also in other regions around the world. We've tried adding more than two units to our cart on the Apple Stores for Japan, Spain and the United Kingdom, in addition to the US, and we've received a warning notice across all the online stores. The notification said: "A maximum of 2 iPhone Duo can be purchased per customer. Please adjust the total quantity of iPhone Duo in your order before checking out." It didn't matter what configuration we tried to purchase — we got the same warning if we had more than two units in our cart.

As MacRumors reports, it's not clear when Apple put the limit in place. According to people on Reddit's iPhone Duo community , some customers were able to place an order for more than two when the company started taking pre-orders on October 16. It's also unclear if and how the company is preventing scalpers from buying more than two units by creating multiple accounts and using different credit cards. That Apple is implementing a purchase limit doesn't come as a surprise. It previously said that the demand for the iPhone Duo was "nothing short of extraordinary," and it had to push back shipping dates to 2027 soon after pre-orders started.

Sure enough, all the stores we've checked show a shipping estimate of January 22, so you will probably have to wait until next year if you haven't pre-ordered yours yet. Some people have been reporting that their shipping estimates were bumped up to earlier slots than the ones they were originally told, but you may have to look at retailers if you want to get your hands on a unit for the holiday season. Best Buy is still showing us a November 10 pick-up and shipping date for the 512GB Duo and December 14 for the 256GB .

en.title: Mamdani says feds have abdicated on AI, urges New Yorkers to push back
en.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Monday night that New Yorkers must resist the narrative that an AI takeover is inevitable and demand regulations that protect the public and put power back in their hands.
en.body:
Two of New York’s sweethearts, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and activist and “Broad City” star Ilana Glazer, spoke about AI at Webster Hall in Manhattan on Monday night, with Glazer posing questions to the mayor about the future of AI in society.

Mamdani encouraged New Yorkers to resist the overwhelming feeling that AI is inevitably coming for their jobs, their kids’ minds, and their dignity, and to take back control instead.

His message came at a moment when the federal government is doing little to regulate AI, leaving cities to act on their own. At The People’s AI Assembly, an event hosted by the AI Now Institute , a think tank that explores the social implications of AI, Mamdani argued that the technology’s rapid rollout is not inevitable and that public officials should hold AI companies accountable.

Last month, Mamdani ordered a ban on AI use in elementary and middle schools. Glazer, a parent, said the technology’s arrival in classrooms unsettles her.

“It just makes me nervous. It feels so non-consensual, as though…this has to be in schools. It wasn’t two years ago. Why does it have to be in schools?” she said.

Over the summer, the mayor also introduced a policy that would require landlords, brokers, and real estate platforms to clearly disclose when a property’s listing photos or videos are made with AI. The policy is aimed at protecting New Yorkers from getting “house-phished,” or tricked by misleading listings.

Both moves challenge the assumption that schools and the public must simply accept AI as it arrives.

“Nothing has to be,” Mamdani said at the event Monday. “There’s a creep that comes with this, and there’s an intent to overwhelm that leaves people feeling as if there is simply no option.”

He said there has been a “reckless adoption of technology without any kind of a reckoning with the limitations of that technology,” citing the U.S. military’s February strike on a school in Iran that killed more than 150 people, including at least 123 children . Officials involved in the Pentagon’s internal investigation have told Bloomberg that overreliance on AI in targeting was one factor in the attack.

“There is this desire to speak about [AI] as if it is infallible, as if it cannot be questioned, as if the only people who can regulate it are the ones who are currently developing it,” Mamdani said, noting that Facebook made similar arguments back in 2008. “What it really is,’ he continued, “is an attempt to escape any kind of accountability at any level, without also jeopardizing the potential valuation from an IPO.”

Anthropic is expected to debut on the public markets this year, and OpenAI has said it will go public in 2027.

Mamdani criticized the “complete abdication of federal law” when it comes to AI.

“At a national level, when the conversation is about artificial intelligence, it’s so often framed in this language of an arms race with China, and any of the humanistic concern, we just push to the side in a language of national competition,” the mayor said.

President Donald Trump’s Superintelligence Task Force , announced earlier this month, largely focuses on allowing powerful AI companies to self-regulate, rather than creating new federal restrictions. That comes despite growing fears about AI’s effect on every facet of human life, including warnings from whistleblowers at Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI that AI could lead to human extinction.

“As we are looking at what comes after this federal administration, there has to be a very different kind of framework in how we think about AI, talk about AI, the accountability we’re willing to bring forward when it comes to that,” Mamdani said.

en.title: How to stop audio from auto-playing on Android Auto
en.summary: Although Android Auto's autoplay feature is intended to be a convenience, you may find yourself wanting to turn it off. Here's how.
en.body:
Because you probably don't want your stereo on at full blast the moment you start your car.

If you've ever started your car only to be blasted by music you didn't ask for, you already know the headache of Android Auto's autoplay quirk. The moment your phone connects, by USB or wirelessly (even if you use an adapter ), your last playlist, podcast or audiobook picks up where it left off at whatever volume you had set the last time you were in the car. It's an unwelcome surprise during a morning commute and a real distraction if you prefer a few quiet seconds before pulling out of the driveway. Depending on what music or audiobooks you were listening to, it may also not be content you want the kids to hear when you're driving them to school.

In the past, fixing this problem was quite difficult and required a ton of workarounds, extra apps and jumping through hoops you really shouldn't have to. Now, it often just requires flipping a toggle.

You'll need to start with Android Auto's own settings. You'll need to go to Settings > Connected devices > Android Auto and look under the Startup section. That's where you'll find the toggle for the Start music automatically feature. If you have trouble finding it, try searching for Android Auto in your settings. Switching this feature off tells Android Auto not to resume playback the moment it connects to your car. For loads of drivers, this single step solves the problem, and it's the first fix mentioned on Spotify's support forums.

If the toggle doesn't help, the issue may be happening at the Bluetooth level rather than inside Android Auto. Android Auto uses Bluetooth to route phone calls and to create the initial handshake between phone and car. One workaround to test is removing your phone from the car's Bluetooth memory and reconnecting with USB only, if your setup allows it. In some vehicles, that can reduce unwanted playback triggers, though results vary by car, phone and connection type.

If you've already disabled Start music automatically and Spotify still starts on its own, you're not imagining things. Spotify users have reported this exact issue across community forums for years, with threads dating back to 2022 that remain active today. But it's worth noting that sometimes your car may not even be to blame at all. Any Bluetooth device paired with your phone, like headphones and speakers, can affect autoplay. According to Spotify's support team, the behavior depends on how a given Bluetooth device interacts with Spotify's API.

That distinction matters because Spotify cannot always prevent a connected device from sending a "play" command when it reconnects, powers on or resumes a media session. Before blaming your phone or reinstalling the app, check whether autoplay happens only with one Bluetooth device and test it with another speaker, headset or vehicle if possible. Keeping Spotify, your phone's operating system and the device firmware updated may reduce connection glitches, but there is no guaranteed universal fix when the command originates from the Bluetooth accessory.

Since Spotify prioritizes easy connections across thousands of hardware combinations, a universal fix isn't guaranteed anytime soon. Some drivers find success through Android Auto's settings, others through Spotify's app permissions and plenty report that neither option works consistently for their specific car or phone. If nothing pans out, you could just remove Spotify from Android Auto entirely, but that means that you won't be able to access Spotify from your car's display.

The bottom line is that you should start with Android Auto's Start music automatically toggle since it resolves the issue for many drivers. If music still plays uninvited, try the Bluetooth unpairing trick before removing the app from Android Auto entirely. Given how inconsistently Bluetooth behaves across car models, expect some trial and error.

en.title: WhatsApp may soon let iPhone users open any link in an in-app browser
en.summary: After introducing limited in-app browser support for certain business links last year, WhatsApp is now working on expanding the feature to all links shared in chats. Here are the details. more…
en.body:
After introducing limited in-app browser support for certain business links last year, WhatsApp is now working on expanding the feature to all links shared in chats. Here are the details.

Last May, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp had begun testing a feature that would allow “users to view certain HTTPS-secured business sites within the app,” with the option to open those links in their default browser via the three-dot menu.

Now, the site reports that WhatsApp is working on extending this support to all in-chat links.

Although the feature is not yet available to beta testers, WABetaInfo has uncovered references to it in the latest TestFlight build and shared screenshots showing how it will work.

According to the site, a new “In-app browser” option under Settings > Chats will let users choose whether links open directly within WhatsApp or in their default browser.

The same settings screen will also let users clear cookies, cache, and other browsing data stored by WhatsApp’s in-app browser.

Here’s WABetaInfo :

Users will be able to enable the in-app browser from the app settings. Here, WhatsApp will add a new option called “In-app browser”. When users enable this feature, they will be able to open any link they send and receive in the chat screen. When users enable this option for the first time, WhatsApp will show a bottom sheet that explains how the feature works. It informs users that they can now open any link within WhatsApp rather than in the default browser. Users will be able to restore the default browser at any time.

The report notes that “WhatsApp cannot see links shared in the conversation and which ones users open.”

As is usually the case with references discovered in WhatsApp’s TestFlight builds, there is currently no word on when the app plans to make the feature available to beta testers or the general public.

To read WABetaInfo ’s full report, follow this link .

en.title: Robot vacuums have a major privacy problem you should be aware of
en.summary: Your robot vacuum's microphone and camera are useful for more efficient cleaning, but it's vital to know how that information is stored and shared.
en.body:
Clean floors shouldn’t come with unclear rules about your personal data.

Depending on the model, a robot vacuum cleaner can potentially generate floor maps, record cleaning histories, watch you take a bathroom break or record your private conversations. Top vacuum models with the most features have various ways to process what's happening inside your home; some include microphones and/or remote video viewing to act as little round drones low-riding on 360-degree wheels. The amount of information they collect and where it goes depends on the model and varies between products.

Cloud connectivity introduces another problem . Robot vacuums that let you check their progress while away from home may communicate through the manufacturer's servers. After all, businesses need to know that you own a Samsung fridge, use DoorDash a lot or accidentally left your dirty skivvies on the floor. Generating a floor map or video is a useful feature, but both are capable of revealing information you'd rather not share with complete strangers.

To be clear, not every connected robot vacuum is secretly recording everything or selling blueprints of your home on eBay. The important takeaway is that there needs to be a clear distinction between data collection and maintaining privacy. Businesses love to bury important information in big block paragraphs of nearly microscopic legalese (the bounded rationality/privacy paradox), but you need to know what is being shared, when and why. Features are fantastic, but that privacy policy is much more important.

Sammy Azdoufal kickstarted a recent robot vacuum controversy. While trying to remotely control his DJI Romo vacuum, he accidentally became the Commander in Chief of roughly 7,000 robot vacuum cleaners across the world. He was able to control and access all these devices instead of just his own.

According to DJI, it resolved the backend permission issue Sammy stumbled into by issuing two updates on February 10, 2026. This was a specific security risk: the server recognized a legitimate customer but failed to restrict that customer to their own device. Sammy used Claude Code to help reverse-engineer the communications, but AI isn't to blame for the underlying security weakness. The failure was in the security checks, which is something a complex password will never fix.

But that's just one story among many. After all, security breaches aren't the only privacy concerns. A shiny new robot vacuum may send information to its manufacturer throughout everyday routines. That could include cleaning activity, device status, floor maps and objects detected. iRobot's privacy policy says connected models may send more data than just floor maps, including room names, floor types, detected objects, the robot's movements and Wi-Fi network details. That's a lot of info, and you may have no idea it's heading out in a steady stream.

There's no clear and established winner here, but a privacy-friendly robot vacuum should at least minimize the amount of information leaving your home. Pore over the privacy policy prior to purchase, and keep an eye out for on-device navigation and image processing features to see what they entail.

Mandatory cloud features should be a deal-breaker, and look for details on how diagnostic data is shared. With a camera-free model, you can at least avoid that degree of exposure, though it may still generate maps and send account information. Keep in mind that "no camera" and "no data collection" are not the same.

For a good local-first approach, Matic is worth a look. Its privacy policy says maps are streamed to the app over home Wi-Fi and processing takes place on the robot. It also identifies exceptions. For example, remote app use can transmit data through an encrypted cloud connection only with explicit consent, and only authorized support can involve sharing audio or video. Those are qualifications worth your consideration.

But remember that while a manufacturer's privacy policy generally describes its commitments, it doesn't serve as proof that the product is unaffected by security flaws. Even if a company doesn't plan to share something, an attacker might still be able to access that existing data.

If you're already using a robot vacuum cleaner, make sure to set a strong password, enable two-factor authentication and keep the firmware up to date. If you see "remote viewing" or other connected features that make you hesitate, disable them unless otherwise needed. Be aware of other robot vacuum downsides , too.

en.title: Accused OpenAI spy had folder called “Saudi Gov Docs,” FBI says
en.summary: US fears Saudi government will help ex-OpenAI engineer flee spying charges.
en.body:
On Monday, a court granted the US government's request to deny release of a former OpenAI engineer accused of bugging a top-secret conference room to steal the frontier lab’s secrets.

In a court filing Sunday, US attorney Craig Missakian argued that Abdulrahman Alfozan must continue to be detained while the US makes its case that Alfozan brazenly spied on OpenAI, either for his own personal business gain or to benefit the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

Evidence showed that Alfozan had been chatting with a member of the KSA royal family on WhatsApp, while pursuing opportunities to permanently move back to Saudi Arabia during the country's biggest AI push yet, the government argued. Shortly before his arrest, the FBI found he accessed a folder called "Saudi Gov Docs" on his iPhone, where he also allegedly stored photos of a second bug he planted in the offices.

en.title: Disney found a way to buy Character.AI without buying its lawsuits
en.summary: Character.AI faces claims its bots encouraged minors to self-harm and kill their parents.
en.body:
This week, Character.AI declared bankruptcy. While some saw the fall of a chatbot platform as a harbinger for the industry , court filings indicate that the decision was actually a key part of a deal that has let Disney hire most of Character.AI’s staff—including its now former CEO Karandeep Anand —potentially acquire most of Character.AI’s technology , and avoid the beleaguered startup’s many legal liabilities and obligations.

In the past few years, Character.AI has faced multiple private lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots, as well as investigations from regulators around the world. In a declaration filed as part of the bankruptcy, Character.AI’s newly appointed CEO explained that the goal of the bankruptcy was to reach a “consensual resolution” with personal injury claimants and a group of states investigating the company, while maximizing the value of the company’s assets for shareholders.

The Disney deal seems to be structured so that whatever is left of Character.AI will retain responsibility for those legal battles, some of which are still ongoing.

Read full article

es.title: NaviLens llega al transporte público de Melbourne para mejorar la accesibilidad de las personas ciegas
es.summary: Vision Australia ha destacado el uso de NaviLens en la red de tranvías de Melbourne. Esta tecnología permite localizar señalización mediante el móvil y recibir información del transporte en audio, texto y respuesta háptica. La iniciativa toma como referencia la ruta 96 y abre el debate sobre cómo mejorar la orientación de las personas con […] La entrada NaviLens llega al transporte público de Melbourne para mejorar la accesibilidad de las personas ciegas se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Vision Australia ha destacado el uso de NaviLens en la red de tranvías de Melbourne. Esta tecnología permite localizar señalización mediante el móvil y recibir información del transporte en audio, texto y respuesta háptica.

La iniciativa toma como referencia la ruta 96 y abre el debate sobre cómo mejorar la orientación de las personas con discapacidad visual en el transporte público.

Vision Australia incluyó NaviLens en su boletín de tecnología de septiembre de 2026. La organización explica que el sistema ayuda a las personas ciegas o con baja visión a orientarse en la red de tranvías de Melbourne mediante códigos instalados en las paradas.

Estos códigos tienen un diseño visual distintivo y pueden detectarse con la cámara del teléfono móvil. A través de la aplicación, el usuario recibe información sobre el servicio en formatos adaptados a sus necesidades.

El sistema puede proporcionar información mediante audio, texto y respuesta háptica, como vibraciones del teléfono. De esta manera, la persona puede acceder a información del entorno sin depender exclusivamente de los carteles convencionales.

La tecnología no requiere que el usuario enfoque el código como haría con un código QR tradicional. Está diseñada para detectarlo a distancia y mientras se mueve, lo que puede facilitar la localización de señales en espacios concurridos.

La utilidad de NaviLens va más allá de identificar una parada. En el proyecto de Melbourne, los códigos se integran con los sistemas de información de Yarra Trams para ofrecer datos dinámicos sobre los servicios.

Entre sus aplicaciones se encuentran:

Estas posibilidades pueden contribuir a que las personas con discapacidad visual planifiquen sus desplazamientos con mayor autonomía. Sin embargo, NaviLens es una herramienta de apoyo: no sustituye la necesidad de contar con itinerarios accesibles, información fiable y asistencia cuando sea necesaria.

El despliegue de NaviLens en el transporte público de Victoria comenzó en agosto de 2023. Según la documentación del propio sistema, el primer código se instaló en la parada 9, en el cruce de Bourke Street y Spring Street.

La ruta 96, que conecta Brunswick East con St Kilda Beach, fue la primera línea piloto. NaviLens documenta la instalación de más de 3.000 códigos en sus marquesinas y en la flota de tranvías E-Class.

Posteriormente, Yarra Trams anunció la ampliación de la tecnología a más paradas y vehículos de su red. La compañía explicó que el objetivo era mejorar el acceso a la información para los pasajeros ciegos o con baja visión.

No obstante, existe una diferencia entre las fuentes consultadas: el boletín de Vision Australia de septiembre de 2026 indica que el servicio está disponible actualmente en la ruta 96 y que se espera extenderlo a otras rutas. Por su parte, la documentación de NaviLens y Yarra Trams describe una ampliación de los códigos a más vehículos y servicios.

Por este motivo, no conviene afirmar que toda la red dispone actualmente de la misma cobertura. La información disponible confirma el despliegue inicial en la ruta 96 y la extensión a determinados vehículos, pero el alcance actual completo requiere una confirmación más específica del operador.

La tecnología no es nueva en España. NaviLens ya se utiliza en distintos sistemas de transporte público, con aplicaciones adaptadas a las necesidades de cada red.

En Barcelona, Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) utiliza estos códigos en estaciones de metro y paradas de autobús. La información puede incluir el nombre y el código de la parada, las líneas disponibles, el destino de los autobuses, los tiempos de llegada y las posibles incidencias.

En las estaciones de metro, los códigos también pueden describir distintos espacios y servicios, como accesos, vestíbulos, ascensores, andenes y puntos de embarque. Esta información ayuda a las personas con discapacidad visual a orientarse durante sus desplazamientos.

El caso de Melbourne resulta interesante porque muestra cómo la tecnología puede integrarse en la señalización del transporte y conectarse con información operativa actualizada. No se trata únicamente de identificar un lugar, sino de facilitar información útil para tomar decisiones durante el viaje.

La experiencia de Melbourne permite reflexionar sobre una cuestión importante: para que el transporte público sea accesible, no basta con disponer de vehículos adaptados o recorridos sin barreras físicas. También es necesario que las personas puedan localizar las paradas, identificar los servicios y consultar los cambios que se producen durante el trayecto.

Los códigos NaviLens pueden contribuir a cubrir parte de esa necesidad al añadir información digital accesible a la señalización física existente. Además, su uso mediante teléfonos móviles permite ofrecer diferentes formatos de información desde un mismo punto.

Para valorar su impacto real, también es importante analizar la cobertura de los códigos, la actualización de los datos, la facilidad de uso de la aplicación y la experiencia de las propias personas ciegas o con baja visión.

La accesibilidad del transporte público depende de soluciones que funcionen en situaciones reales. Iniciativas como la de Melbourne y las implantaciones españolas muestran cómo la tecnología puede ayudar a reducir las barreras de información y favorecer desplazamientos más autónomos.

es.title: Ya disponible la sexta beta de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 6 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la sexta beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la sexta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 6 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 6 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 407cd4afb19d72b533c7a88a7eda86fb38d8aa753134b1000a4b6f6275fc172d. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la sexta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: CoreAI Zoo
en.summary: CoreAI Zoo puts the open-weight AI model zoo on your iPhone, iPad and Mac. Pick a model, download it once, and run it entirely on your device. No account, no server, and nothing you type, say or photograph ever leaves the device. CHAT Stream answers from open language models such as Qwen3, Gemma, LFM2.5, Granite and Mistral, from 0.6B to 30B+ parameters depending on your device's memory. Vision-language models (Qwen3-VL, MiniCPM-V, LFM2.5-VL) answer questions about your photos. VISION Ask questions about an image, read text with on-device OCR, and describe what the camera sees. AUDIO Transcribe speech with Whisper large-v3-turbo, Parakeet and Qwen3-ASR. Talk to an audio-understanding model, generate speech with Kokoro and VoxCPM, and try on-device music generation. CAMERA Live depth estimation, object detection (YOLOX, RF-DETR), action recognition and super-resolution on the camera feed. TOOLS Experimental models such as diffusion-based language models. BENCH Measure load time, tokens per second and memory for any chat model on your own hardware. HOW IT WORKS Every model runs through Core ML on Apple silicon. Weights are downloaded from the Hugging Face Hub on first use over HTTPS, then cached, so the app works offline afterwards. One model is resident at a time to stay within memory limits. New models arrive through a live catalog without an app update. GETTING STARTED Start with Qwen3-0.6B (454 MB) for the fastest first run. Larger models state the free space and memory they need; a recent iPhone Pro or an Apple silicon Mac runs the mid-size ones comfortably. Model weights follow their own licenses, listed on each model's Hugging Face page. The app itself is BSD-3-Clause and part of the open CoreAI model zoo. Report issues and request models at github.com/john-rocky/coreai-model-zoo.

en.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
en.summary: The outside watchdog can publish its findings without Anthropic's approval.
en.body:
Anthropic has granted external evaluators “employee-like access” to assess the risks of its models, following through on a commitment to increase safeguards over concerns the technology could run catastrophically out of control.

METR, a nonprofit that has worked with leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta, now has a team embedded in the Claude maker’s office with access to its hardware and internal systems.

A greater role for third-party evaluators is among the main concrete steps the labs have proposed in response to rising concern about the dangers more capable AI systems could pose to the economy, cyber security, and humanity at large.

en.title: Life In Nature
en.summary: An immersive 3D audio survival game. Craft, hunt, and explore a ruined world. Important: This is an audiogame. The game is played entirely with sound…
en.body:
Published 18 October 2026 by neirin

An immersive 3D audio survival game. Craft, hunt, and explore a ruined world.

Important: This is an audiogame. The game is played entirely with sound and has no visuals. It is designed for the blind and visually impaired community. The screen will be black during gameplay—this is intentional. Headphones are recommended for the best experience.

After a global escalation in science and military technology, the world powers engaged in a catastrophic war. Nuclear explosions altered Earth’s atmosphere, and massive solar storms destroyed all electronic systems. Most of the planet flooded, leaving survivors with only medieval-level resources to endure the harsh new world.

Developed by AudioWander, Life in Nature is a fully 3D spatial-audio multiplayer game specifically designed with accessibility in mind for blind and visually impaired players. In this unforgiving world, survival is your only goal.

Survive the Wild

Every step you take matters. You must carefully manage your Health, Energy, Hunger, and Thirst. Gather wood to build fires, hunt wild animals like bears, boars, and wolves, butcher their meat, and cook it on a skillet or spit. Find fresh water, boil it in a handmade clay pot, and make tea to restore your energy. But beware—falling from heights, animal attacks, or severe hunger will slowly drain your life.

Deep Crafting System

With electronics gone, you must rely on your hands. Gather raw materials from the earth to craft essential tools. Combine items in your hands to weave fishing nets, forge swords and crossbows, or build a sturdy wooden shelter to protect yourself. From a simple stone spear to a complex boat to cross the oceans, everything is built from scratch.

Explore Unique Maps

Navigate entirely by sound and compass directions (North, South, East, West). Explore diverse environments including the Central Valley, dense Bear and Rain forests, scorching deserts, snowy mountain peaks, and deep oceans. Dive underwater to collect oysters or explore hidden caves. Listen closely to your environment—the sound of your footsteps and the ambient noise will guide you.

Challenging Quests & Puzzles

Embark on dangerous quests like “The Lost Miner,” “A Curious Bloom,” or “The Coral Crown.” Jump across perilous chasms, climb steep cliffs, dive into deep underwater tunnels, and search for lost notes and ancient treasures hidden across the world.

Multiplayer & Combat

You are not alone in this ruined world. Meet other survivors, trade resources, and communicate via radio. If you feel brave, activate “PK Mode” (Player Kill) or join or create PK arenas to engage in high-risk, high-reward PvP combat using swords, shotguns, and shields. Team up with trusted friends to hunt dangerous predators or survive the deadly PK map.

Key Features

Put your headphones on, sharpen your senses, and start your new Life in Nature.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

When you launch the game for the first time, it will begin downloading the sounds required to play. Keep your screen reader active during this process so you can hear the download progress. If you leave the game window for any reason, the download will pause until you return.

Once the sounds have finished downloading, the game will launch. At this point, you can disable your screen reader because the game is fully self-voiced.

During account creation, there is a button that sends an account verification code to your email address. After requesting the code, reactivate your screen reader, open your email, copy the verification code, return to the game, paste it into the appropriate field, and then disable your screen reader again.

You can also use a Bluetooth keyboard if the touch gestures are difficult to use. Keyboard shortcuts are available directly from the main menu.

Before playing, make sure you read the rules in their entirety. After finishing the rules, perform a two-finger swipe down with your screen reader to locate the Accept button.

The main menu includes a button for purchasing credits. When you double-tap this button, reactivate your screen reader because the game opens Chrome or your default web browser to complete the transaction through PayPal or another supported payment service.

2.24. Android 16

en.title: Sortalis
en.summary: Sortalis is a dice-building roguelike inspired by Farkle. Roll, score, and decide how far you’re willing to push your luck—then spend your winnings on Charms and upgrades that transform your dice, strengthen your strategy, and rewrite the rules. We’ve got a bumper edition for you this week, with new content for just about everyone!

NV Access is very pleased to announce the release of a new training package. Accessibility Testing with NVDA is designed for people using NVDA to test apps and websites for accessibility.

This Accessibility Testing with NVDA package includes: A training module with over 60 topics in nine sections Getting Started Setting up NVDA Reading information Visual Options Keyboard navigation Navigating content with NVDA Working with elements Testing with a screen reader Reporting Issues A printable NVDA Reference Sheet, with the commands most useful for accessibility testing A printable guide to writing accessible content on a single, printable sheet for easy consultation A list of NV Access and external resources and links to further your knowledge A WCAG 2.2 Reference with tips on testing many of the criteria with NVDA A JPG Badge you can proudly display in your email, or on your website or elsewhere to indicate your support

The purchase price of the module is A$250 (+GST for Australian buyers). Not only do you get a wealth of accessibility testing information, the cost of this package also supports the work of NV Access and helps continue our ability to provide the NVDA screen reading software free of charge.

Please note that this package is useable by both sighted and screen reader users. It is aimed at professionals wanting to test websites, documents and programs for accessibility. If you would like to learn to use NVDA from scratch as a blind or low vision screen reader user, please first consider “ Basic Training for NVDA ” or the “ NVDA Productivity Bundle “.

The Accessibility Testing with NVDA module is designed to teach you to incorporate NVDA into your accessibility testing workflow. It is not intended to replace dedicated accessibility testing tools which can give specific information about testing criteria and compliance etc. If you would like more formal training specifically in web accessibility, we recommend Learn.Intopia.digital . Intopia provided feedback on the web accessibility components of this material.

Please head to Accessibility Testing with NVDA to read more and purchase the new package.

Cover image of “Accessibility Testing with NVDA”

The NVDA Satisfaction Survey 2026 is open, but only until early next week.

We are always interested in understanding the satisfaction of our NVDA users, what is important to you & what we can do more effectively. The survey is anonymous & we encourage you to leave comments in your response.

We’re interested in hearing from as many people as possible, so please feel free to pass this on to others.

The survey is short, only three questions – we deliberately do that in order to make it less onerous to fill out. The rating is a simple, and industry standard metric (a “net promoter score”) we can use to benchmark broadly how well we are doing compared to previous years. We leave room for you to add your own thoughts, so you can give feedback on that one specific point on your mind. If you want a response, please do include your email address as we don’t otherwise collect contact details.

We do sometimes get questions like “It would be great if NVDA had feature X” and it’s frustrating to not be able to reply, especially when NVDA does in fact have feature X, but we have no way to reach the person to share that with them. We have also been asked “Why don’t you ask more questions about X, Y, or Z?” – which is a great question. This survey is designed to collect feedback on everything overall, and we try to keep it fairly consistent from year to year. We do conduct specific surveys from time to time, both more formally, and occasionally just a simple question on Mastodon asking, “What do you think about …”. We like to think we are approachable and easy to get in contact with, so do please always reach out if there is something you’d like to give feedback on or to ask.

Please do head over to https://www.nvaccess.org/survey2026 and fill out the survey if you haven’t already.

We are always looking for ways to help users and make more information available, and easy to find. For many years, the navbar of the NV Access website has had a “Get Help” option. This has linked to a single page of really useful information for NVDA users , including the training material, user groups, how to report an issue or get extra voices, and an FAQ. Now, we have expanded it to a menu. The first item lets you get help for “NVDA Users” and is the original “Get Help” item.

There are also several new options, which are covered below:

With the release of the magnifier in NVDA 2026.2, it seemed a good time to collate some of the features and settings in NVDA which can be useful for low vision users. The way low vision users will have NVDA setup may be different to how a totally blind user who does not use the screen may have it setup. This “ Get Help for Low Vision Users ” page includes information about: The magnifier: including a demo video, list of keystrokes, and link to the comparison with Windows Magnifier we did here in In-Process. Visual Highlighter: How to turn it on and just what the different colours mean. How to reduce speech: Turning on or off individual elements, or adjusting the speech mode overall. Working on the Web: Tips for navigating web pages, and copying information from the web. Other Windows Settings: Suggestions for other Windows settings which can be useful for low vision users.

To go with the brand-new Accessibility Testing with NVDA package , we have made a free sample of the material available. This extensive sample is full of web accessibility tips and tricks with the world’s favourite free screen reader, and is still only a small taste of the full product.

Do check out the Accessibility Testing with NVDA sample page in the new revamped “Get Help” menu. If you find it useful, you will find even more in the full Accessibility Testing with NVDA package , plus you will be supporting us to keep NVDA available for free to everyone who can use it.

Once again, our thanks to Intopia.Digital for their ongoing support of NV Access.

Finally, this week, we’re now up to Beta 5 of NVDA 2026.3 . Last In-Process we were up to Beta 2, so here’s what’s been in the latest three updates:

Changes introduced in Beta 5: Updates to translations Added bug fix for NVDA failing to start on Windows versions older than Windows 10 1903

Changes introduced in Beta 4: Updates to translations Added bug fix for lag in the Add-on Store when searching using Chinese characters Minor documentation changes

Changes introduced in Beta 3: Updates to translations Reverted bug fix to terminals, meaning NVDA may freeze again when substantial amounts of text are dumped to the screen. This is due to the bug fix not working correctly Prevented Magnifier crash recovery from flashing to reduce seizure risk

That’s all for this week. It’s not often the latest beta gets bumped to the SIXTH article in the blog! That by no means reflects on its value though – Please do try NVDA 2026.3 Beta 5 if you haven’t already. If you do any web accessibility work, please do check out the new Accessibility Testing with NVDA Package . It will be around release time for NVDA 2026.3 by next edition, so we’ll have more on the new version. And we’ll also cover a bit more for our low vision users as well.

es.title: Un nuevo prototipo busca llevar el Braille electrónico a restaurantes museos y puntos de información
es.summary: Un equipo de estudiantes de Shawnee State University ha desarrollado una línea Braille electrónica actualizable para facilitar el acceso a la información en espacios públicos. El proyecto continúa en desarrollo y sus creadores trabajan para mejorar el dispositivo y reducir sus costes de fabricación. Una línea Braille para consultar información en espacios públicos Dos estudiantes […] La entrada Un nuevo prototipo busca llevar el Braille electrónico a restaurantes museos y puntos de información se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Un equipo de estudiantes de Shawnee State University ha desarrollado una línea Braille electrónica actualizable para facilitar el acceso a la información en espacios públicos. El proyecto continúa en desarrollo y sus creadores trabajan para mejorar el dispositivo y reducir sus costes de fabricación.

Dos estudiantes de Ingeniería Informática y Tecnologías de Computación de Shawnee State University, en Estados Unidos, han creado un prototipo de línea Braille electrónica que podría facilitar el acceso a información en lugares como restaurantes, museos y puntos de información.

Los estudiantes Parker Lauders y Kade Dancy desarrollaron el dispositivo como proyecto final de sus estudios universitarios. Su objetivo es ofrecer una alternativa a los materiales en Braille impresos, especialmente en espacios donde la información cambia con frecuencia.

La propuesta utiliza tecnología Braille actualizable. En lugar de recurrir a textos impresos de forma permanente, el dispositivo emplea puntos mecánicos que suben y bajan para representar diferentes caracteres. Así, el contenido puede modificarse electrónicamente sin tener que producir un nuevo material en relieve cada vez que cambia la información.

Uno de los ejemplos que plantean sus creadores es el de los restaurantes. Los menús pueden cambiar varias veces al año, por lo que mantenerlos disponibles en Braille requiere actualizar e imprimir nuevos materiales.

Con una pantalla electrónica como esta, el establecimiento podría cargar el contenido actualizado en el dispositivo. De este modo, las personas ciegas podrían consultar la información en Braille sin depender exclusivamente de cartas impresas que pueden quedarse desactualizadas.

La misma idea podría aplicarse a museos, quioscos informativos y otros espacios públicos en los que se ofrecen datos sobre servicios, exposiciones o indicaciones.

El planteamiento busca que la información accesible sea más fácil de mantener y actualizar. No obstante, su utilidad real dependerá de cómo se implemente el sistema en cada entorno y de que el contenido esté disponible en un formato adecuado para las personas usuarias.

La idea surgió cuando Parker Lauders era estudiante de primer año. Tras varios años de formación práctica, él y Kade Dancy consiguieron diseñar, construir y programar un prototipo funcional como parte de su proyecto final.

El trabajo combina componentes electrónicos, programación y piezas mecánicas fabricadas específicamente para el dispositivo. Según la documentación académica del proyecto, el sistema incorpora 20 celdas Braille personalizadas y un microcontrolador STM32.

Aunque el proyecto ha permitido desarrollar y probar distintos componentes del sistema, todavía existen aspectos técnicos que deben mejorarse, especialmente en el mecanismo encargado de accionar los puntos Braille.

Por ello, sus creadores continúan trabajando en el hardware, la funcionalidad y la reducción de los costes de fabricación. También prevén explorar la protección mediante patente y las posibilidades de llevar la tecnología al mercado.

El proyecto se ha presentado en el Capitolio del Estado de Ohio, una oportunidad para mostrar su potencial más allá del entorno universitario.

Por el momento, no se ha anunciado que el dispositivo esté disponible comercialmente . Se trata de un prototipo universitario en fase de desarrollo, no de un producto que pueda comprarse e instalarse actualmente en restaurantes o museos.

Su evolución será interesante para el ámbito de la accesibilidad, ya que plantea una posible forma de facilitar la actualización de información en Braille en espacios públicos.

Si consigue resolver los retos técnicos pendientes y alcanzar un coste de fabricación asumible, podría abrir nuevas posibilidades para que establecimientos y entidades ofrezcan información accesible de manera más flexible.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

en.title: From Word to Teams: Using ZoomText and Fusion Across Your Workday
en.summary: ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech. Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful …
en.body:
ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech.

Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful features of ZoomText and Fusion that will help you be more productive in the workplace. This blog series will run throughout October, with a new post every Thursday featuring helpful information and practical tips to make the most of ZoomText and Fusion as you work.

For many professionals, the workday is a journey through Microsoft Office and a variety of collaboration tools. Whether you’re writing, analyzing data, managing emails, or joining virtual meetings, having ZoomText or Fusion set up to support your workflow can make all the difference. This week, we’ll look at how these tools can help you work more efficiently and comfortably, from your first document to your last video call.

Drafting reports or editing proposals is easier when you can see exactly what you need. With ZoomText, you can quickly adjust your magnification level or switch between different zoom window types—like Lens or Line view—to focus on the text that matters most. For longer documents, AppReader is a helpful feature: just press CAPS LOCK+ALT+A to have the text read aloud, letting you follow along visually or simply listen and rest your eyes.

Fusion users can also take advantage of JAWS navigation commands, such as jumping between headings or moving by paragraph, to quickly scan and organize content. To jump by heading, first turn on Quick Navigation keys by pressing CAPS LOCK+Z , then press H to navigate forward through headings or SHIFT+H to navigate backward. Press P to navigate forward by paragraph and SHIFT+P to navigate backward. Press CAPS LOCK+Z to toggle Quick Navigation keys off again so you can continue editing your document.

Keyboard Echo is another useful feature, giving you spoken feedback as you type, so you can be sure your edits are accurate.

To cycle through the different Keyboard Echo settings, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+K . The setting No Echo disables all keyboard echo. Keys will echo your keystrokes as you type. Words will echo individual words as you type them. And Keys and Words will echo both keystrokes and words as you type.

Spreadsheets can be intimidating, but ZoomText’s magnification tools help you zero in on the data you need. Adjust your zoom to see more or less of your sheet and use Reading Zones to mark important areas—like totals or headers—so you can return to them instantly.

A reading zone is a defined area of an application window that ZoomText can display, speak, or both, at the press of a hotkey. To create a reading zone, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+C , then drag a rectangle over the area of the application window you want the zone to cover. To trigger a reading zone, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+ the zone’s number (1 through 9, or 0 for zone 10).

Fusion users can rely on JAWS table navigation to move efficiently through rows and columns, with commands like CAPS LOCK+C to read the current cell, helping you keep your place in complex data.

Staying on top of emails and appointments is simple with the right tools. AppReader lets you listen to long emails, while Focus Enhancements in ZoomText highlight your current selection, making it easier to track where you are.

AppReader reads documents, web pages, and email aloud while you follow along or rest your eyes. It can read from beginning to end, skim forward and backward, or read just the text you select with the mouse. AppReader reads text aloud in three modes: App View reads directly in the source application without changing your view, Text View reformats the text with your choice of fonts, colors, and magnification for easier reading, and the SpeakIt Tool reads any text on the screen that you select by clicking and dragging. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+A to launch App View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+T to launch Text View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+S to launch the SpeakIt Tool.

Focus enhancements highlight the item you are on as you navigate using the Tab and arrow keys through menus, dialogs, and toolbars, making it easy to keep your place. Press CAPS LOCK+F to toggle focus enhancements on and off.

Fusion users can use commands like CTRL+N to create a new message, CTRL+R to reply to a message, or CTRL+F to forward a message. You can also switch to different areas in Outlook with quick shortcuts like CTRL+1 to go to your current mail folder, CTRL+2 to navigate to the calendar, and CTRL+3 to go to Contacts.

Whether you’re building slides or presenting to your team, ZoomText’s flexible magnification ensures you can see every detail. AppReader can read slide content aloud, making it easier to review your work or follow along during a presentation. Fusion users can use the arrow keys with JAWS to navigate slides and read speaker notes, so you’re always prepared and in control. Press F6 in PowerPoint to navigate the different areas of your presentation.

Today’s workplace relies on video conferencing apps like Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Google Meet. With ZoomText and Fusion, you can adjust your magnification to follow chat messages, participant panels, and shared screens during meetings. AppReader and JAWS speech help you keep up with notifications and chat without missing a beat.

A standout feature for video calls is Face-in-View . Before joining a meeting, open the Face-in-View tool in Fusion by pressing INSERT+SPACE, F , then O . This feature uses your webcam to show you a live preview and provides feedback to help you center your face and check your lighting—so you can join every call looking your best and feeling confident.

Join us next week as we explore how ZoomText and Fusion can help you access more online, making web browsing and digital resources easier and more accessible. Stay tuned for more tips to help you thrive in your workplace!

Have questions? Email training@vispero.com .

With the right setup and a few helpful features, ZoomText and Fusion can empower you to work smarter and more comfortably, every step of the way.

es.title: SparkVision Glasses 2: un nuevo modelo de gafas con IA para ceguera y baja visión
es.summary: Las nuevas gafas asistivas de SparkVision leen etiquetas, describen entornos y responden a preguntas mediante inteligencia artificial. Hay dos versiones disponibles, con precios desde 1.500 euros. Las gafas inteligentes con inteligencia artificial siguen ganando terreno en el ámbito de la accesibilidad visual. Una de las propuestas más recientes es SparkVision Glasses 2, una familia de […] La entrada SparkVision Glasses 2: un nuevo modelo de gafas con IA para ceguera y baja visión se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Las nuevas gafas asistivas de SparkVision leen etiquetas, describen entornos y responden a preguntas mediante inteligencia artificial. Hay dos versiones disponibles, con precios desde 1.500 euros.

Las gafas inteligentes con inteligencia artificial siguen ganando terreno en el ámbito de la accesibilidad visual. Una de las propuestas más recientes es SparkVision Glasses 2 , una familia de gafas diseñadas para ayudar a las personas ciegas y con baja visión a acceder a información visual mediante respuestas habladas.

La empresa búlgara SparkVision ha presentado esta nueva generación en demostraciones presenciales y eventos tecnológicos durante septiembre de 2026. Sin embargo, hay una diferencia importante respecto a otras novedades del sector: las gafas ya aparecen a la venta en la tienda oficial de la compañía .

La gama incluye dos versiones, con diferentes prestaciones y precios. Según la tienda oficial, ambas se comercializan con IVA incluido.

Ambas versiones incluyen el anillo inteligente SparkVision Smart Ring, que permite controlar funciones sin tener que manipular continuamente las gafas.

La compañía ofrece información de compra en su tienda oficial . También indica que realiza envíos a los países de la Unión Europea cuando existe disponibilidad para la dirección o modalidad de entrega seleccionada.

No obstante, antes de comprar desde España conviene confirmar el plazo de entrega, las condiciones de envío y las prestaciones incluidas en cada paquete.

El objetivo de SparkVision Glasses 2 es convertir información visual en respuestas habladas. Para ello, incorporan una cámara, micrófonos y un sistema de control integrado en la montura.

Estas son algunas de sus funciones principales.

Las gafas pueden reconocer textos impresos y reproducirlos mediante voz. Esta función puede ser útil para consultar cartas de restaurantes, envases, etiquetas de productos, recibos y documentos cotidianos.

También ofrecen lectura de varias páginas y herramientas para facilitar el posicionamiento de los textos frente a la cámara.

Otra de las funciones anunciadas es la descripción del entorno. El usuario puede obtener información hablada sobre lo que aparece delante de la cámara y utilizar el asistente para preguntar sobre una escena.

El sistema también incorpora una función para buscar objetos. El usuario indica qué quiere localizar y recibe orientación hablada para encontrarlo dentro del campo de visión.

Estas posibilidades pueden facilitar algunas tareas cotidianas, aunque las respuestas de la inteligencia artificial pueden ser incorrectas o incompletas.

Las gafas también incluyen herramientas para identificar colores, detectar luz y reconocer billetes.

La versión Ultra añade funciones como el recuento estimado de dinero visible y la lectura de información presente en los recibos. Como sucede con otros sistemas de reconocimiento visual, es importante comprobar los resultados antes de realizar pagos o tomar decisiones económicas.

SparkVision Glasses 2 incorpora un asistente de IA para responder preguntas y ofrecer información sobre el entorno.

Además, permite iniciar una llamada a una persona de confianza previamente elegida. Durante esa llamada, el usuario puede compartir la perspectiva de la cámara para recibir ayuda humana cuando la inteligencia artificial no sea suficiente.

La posibilidad de recurrir a una persona es especialmente interesante en situaciones en las que una descripción automática no proporciona toda la información necesaria.

La diferencia entre las dos versiones no se limita al precio.

SparkVision Glasses 2 Ultra incorpora funciones adicionales de orientación y acceso a información durante los desplazamientos. Entre ellas se encuentran la navegación asistida y la consulta de información sobre transporte público, como paradas, líneas y salidas.

También incluye una batería externa que, según el fabricante, permite alcanzar hasta 12 horas de uso, dependiendo de las condiciones y del modo utilizado. La versión Lite anuncia hasta cuatro horas de uso activo.

El equipo pesa aproximadamente 38,5 gramos, según las especificaciones técnicas publicadas por SparkVision. La cámara integrada tiene una resolución de 12 megapíxeles y la conectividad incluye Wi-Fi 6 y Bluetooth 5.3.

No todas las funciones dependen necesariamente de la nube, pero tampoco conviene afirmar que las gafas funcionan completamente sin Internet.

El manual oficial explica que determinados procesos se realizan localmente, mientras que otros utilizan la aplicación SparkVision Assistant y los servicios de la compañía. Las funciones en línea pueden transmitir datos a los servicios de SparkVision o a proveedores de procesamiento.

La aplicación complementaria está destinada a Android, según la documentación técnica. Por eso, antes de adquirirlas, conviene comprobar la compatibilidad con el teléfono y las funciones que requieren conexión o acceso adicional.

Las gafas de inteligencia artificial pueden facilitar el acceso a información visual, pero es importante conocer sus límites.

SparkVision advierte en su manual que el dispositivo no debe utilizarse como único apoyo para desplazarse en entornos peligrosos. Tampoco debe confiarse exclusivamente en sus respuestas para cruzar calles, acercarse a vehículos o tomar decisiones relacionadas con la seguridad.

Estas herramientas deben entenderse como un complemento a los apoyos habituales de movilidad y accesibilidad, no como un sustituto del bastón blanco, del perro guía o de las técnicas de orientación y movilidad.

También es recomendable tener en cuenta la privacidad. Las gafas incorporan cámara y micrófonos, por lo que su utilización debe respetar la intimidad de las personas y las normas aplicables a la captación de imágenes y sonido.

La propuesta de SparkVision destaca por reunir lectura de textos, reconocimiento de objetos, descripción de escenas y asistencia mediante IA en un dispositivo portátil.

La versión Lite ofrece un conjunto de funciones básicas por 1.500 euros, mientras que la Ultra amplía las posibilidades de orientación y transporte público por 5.566 euros. La diferencia de precio es considerable, por lo que conviene comparar las necesidades de cada usuario con las funciones realmente incluidas.

Por ahora, la información oficial confirma que las dos versiones forman parte de la oferta comercial de SparkVision , aunque la disponibilidad concreta y los plazos de entrega deben comprobarse durante el proceso de compra.

Para las personas ciegas y con baja visión interesadas en nuevas herramientas de asistencia visual, estas gafas son una opción que merece seguimiento, especialmente por la combinación de lectura, descripción del entorno y posibilidad de contactar con una persona de confianza.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

es.title: Ya disponible la quinta beta de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 5 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la quinta beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la quinta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 5 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 5 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es c1d2cc7bc21126a224fdc0733fef5f20adf212d6098fd31863c89f7d05195544. ¡Feliz miércoles!

La entrada Ya disponible la quinta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
