en.title: Welcome Home: Apple Announces Updated HomePod Mini, Apple TV, All-New HomeView, and New Home Accessories
en.summary: Apple today announced updated models of the HomePod Mini and Apple TV 4K ; as well as an all-new HomeView smart home hub and a collection of smart home accessories . HomePod Mini 2 Powered by the S10 chip and what Apple calls "advanced computational audio," up to four HomePod Mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation) speakers can be paired to create a surround sound experience with the new Apple TV 4K. Siri AI will be available on HomePod Mini 2 with a future software update. It can recognize up to six people in a household, and can use a user's Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone or iPad to draw on their personal context. With Sound Glow, the top of HomePod Mini 2 can glow and pulse in sync with the currently playing song. Users can additionally customize the displayed animations to promote a relaxing atmosphere. HomePod Mini 2 features 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, and 100 percent recycled copper, gold plating, and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today in pink, green, blue, white and midnight for US $149, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, October 30. HomeView HomeView is a smart home hub with a speaker and 7-inch display, which can either be placed on a table or mounted on a wall. It features a variety of Apple apps and widgets on the Home Screen, and allows users to play music, view photos and videos, make and receive FaceTime calls, monitor and control their home, and more using Siri or the touch interface. HomeView can display a generic screen for everyone in the household, or recognize up to six faces to show personalized content for individual users. Apple Silicon and HomeView's speaker array can optimize audio for loudness and bass response at any volume, with tailored profiles for the table-top and wall-mounted models. Siri AI can be used to play media on HomeView, answer general knowledge questions, discuss recipes, and if a user has an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone or iPad, draw on their personal context for more helpful responses. Like other Apple Intelligence-capable devices, conversations with Siri AI on HomeView are synced via iCloud and viewable in the Siri app on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. Changes made to Siri's pace or expressiveness on compatible devices are synced to HomeView. HomeView features a wide variety of watchOS-style faces that can display snippets of information at a glance, a user's photos, or interactive art. With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView can integrate with compatible cameras to recognize people, pets, packages, and vehicles, and can describe captured video using AI. With Sound Recognition, HomeView can alert users to smoke and carbon monoxide detectors on their iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. Similar to the security and privacy features of other Apple products, data processed by the A18 chip's Secure Exclaves is isolated from the HomeView software and does not leave the device. Users' personal content, like messages and calendar, is only displayed when the user's face is recognized and their iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked. The wall-mounted HomeView model can optionally be professionally installed. HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for US $299, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 13. The table-top model is available in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray finishes, with the wall-mounted model available in space gray and silver finishes. Apple TV 4K With the A19 chip, Apple claims the new Apple TV 4K delivers up to 50 percent faster CPU performance and up to 2X faster GPU performance when compared to the previous generation. In addition, a new, dedicated AV1 decoder enables more efficient streaming while using less bandwidth. Continuing on the theme of recent Apple product unveilings, the new Apple TV 4K supports Siri AI for smarter voice interactions. Users can find entertainment and control their smart home with more flexible natural language, and Siri AI's awareness of personal context and onscreen content can be used to answer questions about home events or what's currently playing. Users with an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone or iPad will be able to use Siri AI on Apple TV 4K (2nd and 3rd generation). Three far-field microphones on the new Apple TV 4K support Siri hands-free, allowing users to prompt it by saying "Siri" or "Hey Siri," as they do on other Apple devices. The new Siri Remote supports Find My with Precision Finding, which can guide users to the remote's precise location, useful if it, for example, falls between couch cushions. Like other Find My-capable devices, the remote can also play a sound to help users locate it. Similar to other Apple products, data processed by the Secure Exclaves is isolated from tvOS and does not leave the device. The new Apple TV 4K features 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for US $299, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 13. Home Collection In collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric, Apple has launched a collection of smart home accessories, including a lock, doorbell, thermostats, temperature sensors, and indoor and outdoor cameras. These accessories support NFC for one-tap setup on iPhone, and will begin rolling out in December.
en.body: Apple today announced updated models of the HomePod Mini and Apple TV 4K ; as well as an all-new HomeView smart home hub and a collection of smart home accessories .

en.title: Tindrift: Merge Roguelike
en.summary: One slide moves your whole army. Tindrift is a tactics roguelike built on slide-merge combat: same-class, same-rank soldiers merge into a higher rank, and every shadow acts by rule — no dice, ever. 100 floors across five acts, plus an Endless Drift, a Daily Seed and 1v1 duels. The campaign plays offline. NO LUCK TO BLAME Shadows telegraph the move they are about to make, gates cycle on a visible clock, and pits sit where you can plan around them. When a run ends you can name the exact slide that ended it — and when you win, you out-thought the board. YOU COMMAND AN ARMY, NOT A HERO Six soldier classes — vanguard, tank, medic, marksman, poisoner, support — merge only with their own kind, so every squad trades coverage against raw power. Set the formation before you climb: tank into the crowd, marksman down the long lane, medic in the middle. WHAT IS IN THE GAME • A 5-act campaign across 100 floors — 20 per act, with 3 mini-boss fights and one signature boss in each • The Sunken Tray, The Rusthold, The Shivering Span, The Frostlight, The Surface: five acts, one climb, ending in daylight • 46 synergy blueprints (15 common, 23 uncommon, 8 rare) — pierce a lane, detonate poison chains, strip terrain for scrap, or take a drawback for reach • 24 shadow archetypes, 5 mini-bosses and 5 act bosses among them, each with a rule you have to read before you can answer it • 8 terrain types — sealed exits, timed gates, pits, fog and mazes: the map fights back • 7 kinds of tactic across 8 placeable tools, plus a TINKER STATION between floors to heal, promote, recruit and re-arm • An 18-node cog tree worth 2,335 cog — side-grades and finishes, never raw stats • 22 achievements and 3 daily quests drawn from 7 types • Endless Drift, and a Daily Seed with streaks and a result you can share • 1v1 duels, same seed and separate boards: three bot difficulties offline, or trade a 6-character code with a friend, send sabotage between floors and replay their round • Four languages: English, Turkish, German and Spanish • VoiceOver reads the board and re-announces it after every slide, and hazards are named instead of signalled by colour alone VARIETY UNLOCKS, POWER DOES NOT Nothing here is pay-to-win. Loadouts, tactics and blueprints stay behind cog for every player, and the limits per run are the same for everyone: one continue, two rerolls, three undos. ADS, PLAINLY Rewarded videos are always your choice — five spots, all opt-in. Full-screen breaks land on floor transitions and after a run, at most one every two minutes, never mid-move and never on the way into a boss or mini-boss floor. Duels carry none. TINDRIFT PREMIUM — one purchase, no subscription • Removes every ad • Lets you HOST duel rooms (joining a room is always free) • Unlocks the 10 cosmetics the workshop sells: 8 soldier finishes and 2 tray themes Slide. Merge. Climb.

en.title: Astonischika
en.summary: Astonischika is a turn-based pixel role-playing game with a roguelite loop. Build a party from bold classes, climb a branching map and fight turn by turn against monsters, elites and bosses. Every run is different: you choose your path across battles, rest sites, treasure, merchants and minigames. When your party falls, the city remains your permanent home — your heroes, their gold and their gear grow from run to run. FEATURES • Build your party from a range of classes — warrior, mage, cleric, rogue, archer and more • Turn-based battles with skills, spells, elements and status effects • Branching map: battle, elite, boss, rest, treasure and merchant • Level-ups, attribute points, equipment and learnable spells • Minigames: shell game, dice, memory, coin flip and more • A permanent city hub — your progress stays after every run • Endless scaling for long-term motivation • 22 languages, music and sound effects GREAT FOR Quick battle rounds in between, or long dungeon sessions.

es.title: Orbit Strata 40: la nueva línea Braille de 40 celdas que llegará al mercado en octubre
es.summary: Orbit Research prepara el lanzamiento de una nueva línea Braille portátil con 40 celdas, teclado Perkins y conexión Bluetooth. El dispositivo también permite leer libros y tomar notas sin depender de un ordenador. La tiflotecnología sigue avanzando con nuevas alternativas para acceder a la información mediante el tacto. Una de las novedades previstas para este […] La entrada Orbit Strata 40: la nueva línea Braille de 40 celdas que llegará al mercado en octubre se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Orbit Research prepara el lanzamiento de una nueva línea Braille portátil con 40 celdas, teclado Perkins y conexión Bluetooth. El dispositivo también permite leer libros y tomar notas sin depender de un ordenador.

La tiflotecnología sigue avanzando con nuevas alternativas para acceder a la información mediante el tacto. Una de las novedades previstas para este otoño es el Orbit Strata 40 , una línea Braille diseñada para combinar lectura, escritura y conectividad en un único dispositivo.

La compañía Orbit Research presentó esta familia de productos en marzo de 2026, durante la conferencia CSUN Assistive Technology Conference. Su objetivo es ampliar las opciones disponibles para las personas ciegas que utilizan dispositivos Braille en sus estudios, su trabajo o su vida cotidiana.

No consta que esté disponible para su compra directa .

La página oficial de Orbit Research anuncia que el Strata 40 estará a la venta en octubre de 2026. Sin embargo, a fecha de 10 de octubre, la web sigue ofreciendo un formulario para apuntarse a una lista de espera y recibir un aviso cuando comiencen los envíos.

Por tanto, aunque el lanzamiento está previsto para este mes, no podemos confirmar que ya se esté comercializando ni que se pueda adquirir desde España. La empresa dispone de una red internacional de distribuidores, entre ellos ONCE-CIDAT, pero será necesario consultarles para conocer la disponibilidad y el precio en España.

El precio anunciado por el fabricante es de 2.595 dólares . Esta cifra no debe interpretarse como un precio final en euros, ya que pueden variar los impuestos, los gastos de distribución y las condiciones de venta.

El Orbit Strata 40 incorpora 40 celdas Braille actualizables de ocho puntos , que permiten leer información digital mediante el tacto. A diferencia de los modelos tradicionales de la familia Orbit Reader, este dispositivo utiliza tecnología piezoeléctrica.

El equipo integra un teclado Braille de ocho teclas, con distribución tipo Perkins, y controles de navegación para desplazarse por documentos y menús. También dispone de teclas de posicionamiento del cursor, que permiten situarse directamente en un punto concreto del texto.

Su diseño compacto busca facilitar el transporte y el uso diario. Según las especificaciones oficiales, pesa aproximadamente 600 gramos y mide 30 × 9,5 × 2,8 centímetros.

Una de las características más interesantes del Strata 40 es que puede utilizarse de forma independiente o conectado a un ordenador o teléfono móvil.

En modo autónomo, permite leer libros y documentos, tomar notas y editar archivos. También incorpora herramientas como calendario, reloj, alarma y calculadora.

El dispositivo admite archivos de texto y formatos Braille como BRF y BRL. Además, integra traducción Braille en ambos sentidos para más de 70 idiomas, según el fabricante.

Estas funciones pueden resultar útiles para estudiantes, profesionales y usuarios que quieran consultar documentos o escribir notas sin tener que recurrir constantemente a otro equipo.

El Orbit Strata 40 también funciona como línea Braille externa. Puede conectarse mediante USB-C o Bluetooth a ordenadores y dispositivos móviles compatibles.

Orbit Research indica que es compatible con lectores de pantalla habituales en Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, ChromeOS, Fire OS y Linux. Además, permite mantener conectados hasta cinco dispositivos y cambiar entre ellos.

Esta posibilidad puede facilitar el trabajo de quienes alternan entre el ordenador, el teléfono móvil y otros equipos durante la jornada.

El fabricante también destaca su batería de larga duración, la carga rápida y la resistencia al polvo y a los líquidos. Incluye una ranura para tarjetas SD y permite acceder a archivos almacenados en memorias USB.

La principal diferencia está en la combinación de una línea de 40 celdas, funciones de anotador y tecnología piezoeléctrica en un formato portátil.

La nueva familia Strata también incluye otros modelos. El Strata 40 Pro añade funciones multimedia, síntesis de voz, conectividad Wi-Fi y aplicaciones integradas más amplias. Por su parte, el Strata 20 Pro ofrece un formato de 20 celdas con funciones multimodales.

Conviene no confundirlos: el Strata 40 estándar está pensado para leer, escribir y conectarse con otros equipos, mientras que las versiones Pro amplían las posibilidades con voz, audio y servicios adicionales.

El Orbit Strata 40 es una de las novedades relevantes de la tiflotecnología anunciadas para 2026. Su combinación de lectura Braille, anotación y conectividad puede resultar interesante para quienes buscan un dispositivo portátil para estudiar, trabajar o acceder a documentos digitales.

No obstante, todavía quedan cuestiones prácticas por confirmar para los usuarios en España: la fecha efectiva de los primeros envíos, la disponibilidad a través de distribuidores nacionales y el precio final en euros.

Desde el punto de vista de la accesibilidad, el lanzamiento amplía las alternativas existentes para acceder a la información mediante Braille. Habrá que esperar a conocer su disponibilidad comercial y las condiciones de distribución para valorar su llegada al mercado español.

Estado del producto: lanzamiento anunciado para octubre de 2026; la web oficial sigue indicando que hay que apuntarse a la lista de espera para recibir un aviso cuando comiencen los envíos.

en.title: Paperback
en.summary: Paperback is a fast, fully accessible reader for ebooks, documents and audio books. It opens over twenty formats and speaks sixteen languages. Opening documents: Use…
en.body:
Published 9 October 2026 by Quin

Paperback is a fast, fully accessible reader for ebooks, documents and audio books. It opens over twenty formats and speaks sixteen languages.

Opening documents:

Reading and listening:

Paperback has two ways to read a document. In text mode, you read the text with your screen reader. In read aloud mode, Paperback reads the text to you with the voice you pick in Settings, and keeps going in the background and from the lock screen. Switch between them from the More Options menu. Audio books, like DAISY, M4B, and MP3 books, play their own recording instead.

The reading bar:

The bar at the bottom of the screen has, from left to right:

You can also swipe up or down on the play button to move by the navigation unit, without reaching for the previous and next buttons. If that is all you use, the Hide previous and next buttons setting takes them out of your screen reader’s way. The Swipe up moves forward setting picks which way a swipe goes.

More options

The More Options menu is where everything else lives.

Keyboards and headsets:

With a keyboard, the desktop shortcuts for opening books, recent documents, Find, Go To, the table of contents, word count, document info, export, and the sleep timer all work. So do the single-letter keys for moving by heading, page, link, and the rest, and Space plays and pauses. A headset button plays and pauses with one press, moves forward with two, and goes back with three.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Paperback was designed with screen readers, and works flawlessly with both TalkBack and Backtalk.
