en.title: Apple Releases iOS 27 and iPadOS 27
en.summary: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are now available to the public. (Note: As spotted by AppleVis Community Member TJT 2001 , Apple has also released iOS/iPadOS 26.7 for those not wishing to upgrade to iOS 27.) This post contains Apple's Release Notes for iOS 27, as well as links to all of AppleVis' content related to these updates. Also included are instructions on how to install the update. iOS 27 Release Notes iOS 27 introduces the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, as well as new features to help parents create safe digital experiences for kids, and improvements that make iOS more responsive and delightful to use. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri that is more intelligent, knowledgeable, and capable. The next generation of Apple Intelligence also powers new features across apps that simplify the things you do every day, like editing images in Photos, communicating in Messages and Mail, and browsing in Safari. New parental controls and significant updates to Screen Time make it more intuitive and easy to use, so parents can feel confident that they're building the right digital experience for their child. And with improvements that span design, performance, connectivity, search, and more, the experience on iOS 27 has been refined and elevated, so it feels even better to use. Siri AI (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) A more capable and conversational version of Siri is rolling out to users. It helps you find what you need and get more done, drawing on capabilities like personal context understanding, app actions, onscreen awareness, and access to broad world knowledge. New voice experience offers more expressive and natural-sounding voices, and lets you customize expressivity and pace to make Siri more personal to you using powerful on-device models on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Dedicated Siri app provides an easy way to revisit an existing conversation or kick off a new one, and privately syncs conversations across your Apple products with iCloud. Siri mode in Camera integrates Visual Intelligence into the Camera app, letting you ask questions and take action with what's in front of you, like splitting a bill or looking up nutritional info for a plate of food. Write with Siri enables you to generate a draft from scratch, edit what you've written, or get feedback from Siri virtually anywhere you type. In Messages & Mail, Siri personalizes your writing style based on your relationships, and uses unique phrases and punctuation that you've previously used in your conversations with those people. Apple Intelligence across apps (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) Photos. Spatial Reframing lets you adjust the composition of a photo after it was taken by virtually changing the camera position. Extend tool intelligently expands images beyond their edges with realistic infill, so you can straighten horizons, change aspect ratios, or add more space around a subject. Clean Up supports removing even larger objects, with more realistic, high-quality results, and you can choose between Fast mode for small blemishes or High Quality for more intricate edits. Safari. Organize by Topic uses Apple Intelligence to sort your tabs, analyzing webpages and automatically grouping similar tabs together. Notify Me can periodically check a webpage for updates, like price changes and item availability. Describe an Extension lets you create a custom extension using natural language to adjust your view of a website's content or formatting. All-new Image Playground uses a new generative model to make high-quality images in virtually any style, including photorealistic, lets you modify your images using touch and natural language, and lets you generate Lock Screen wallpapers and Contact Posters with personalized suggestions. Describe a Shortcut lets you use natural language to create a shortcut or refine an existing one. Home. Summarized activity notifications combine related alerts across accessories into a single notification. Video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video recordings summarize what's happening in a clip for eligible iCloud+ subscribers. Camera clip search lets you find specific moments from your HomeKit Secure Video cameras by searching in the Home app or Spotlight when on an eligible iCloud+ plan. Describe an event in Calendar lets you use natural language to create an event, and details like the time, location, invitees, and event title are filled in using Apple Intelligence. Suggestions in Mail help you take action based on the context of your emails, like getting directions to a restaurant you booked. Call Context in the Phone app understands when you're speaking to certain businesses and proactively surfaces relevant information from across your apps, like a confirmation code or a reservation number. Accessibility. VoiceOver enhancements include more detailed and contextual image understanding for photos, charts, and screenshots, a conversational experience that lets you ask questions about your screen or surroundings, and a new way to get answers fast with an Action button integration. An enhanced Magnifier experience offers conversational visual assistance for users with low vision, with a high-contrast interface and natural language app controls for zooming and other Magnifier functions. A smarter Accessibility Reader uses intelligence to provide better text cleanup and formatting, images and tables, on-demand summaries, and translation. Voice Control flexible inputs help you navigate your device with just your voice by describing elements on screen in your own words, like "tap the gear" or "tap the button in the top right". And more, including additional ways to create and modify Genmoji, automatic proofreading, and more accurate dictation using an on-device model on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Child Safety Improved setup experience for new child accounts lets parents choose the exact apps their kids can access when they set up an iPhone for their child. Ask to Browse gives parents the option to approve each new website before their child can view it. Expanded Communication Safety protections help intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos. Time Allowances help parents set boundaries around how long kids can use apps across Entertainment, Games, and Social Media apps, offering guidance based on expert research and tailored to each child's age. Schedules let parents choose which apps their kids can access at different points in their day and across weekdays and weekends. Redesigned Screen Time settings give parents at-a-glance information about how their kids use their devices, and controls to adjust access in just a few taps. System Improvements Liquid Glass refinements improve overall readability, and a new slider in Settings lets you personalize its appearance from ultra-clear to fully tinted . Faster performance in experiences across the system, including app launches, new photos loading in your Photos library, and AirDrop transfers. Improved search provides more relevant and comprehensive results in Spotlight, Photos, and Mail. Connectivity Assist enables more seamless transitions between Wi-Fi and cellular networks. And more improvements across apps and experiences, including enhancements to iCloud Shared Albums in Photos, Custom EQ for AirPods, support for perimenopause and menopause in Cycle Tracking in the Health app, and independent volume settings for Alarms and Timers. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 Some features may not be available in all regions or on all iPhone models. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/ios/feature-availability/ Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/apple-intelligence Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit: https://support.apple.com/125039 AppleVis iOS 27 Content AppleVis has the following content available for iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: Blog Post: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver and Braille Issues and Improvements Blog Post: What's new in Accessibility in iOS 27 for Blind and DeafBlind Users , by Scott Davert Podcast: An Overview of the New VoiceOver and Braille Features in iOS 27 , by Michael Hansen Podcast: A Demonstration of the New Image Description Features in iOS 27 , by David Nason Podcast: A Demonstration and Walk-Through of the New Live Recognition Features in iOS 27 , by Levi Gobin How to Update iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update), via Finder on a Mac with macOS Catalina or later, or via iTunes on a PC or Mac with macOS Mojave or earlier. Before updating, we strongly recommend making a full and complete backup of your device (either locally or in iCloud, depending on personal preference). This will ensure that, in the unlikely event that something goes wrong during the update process, you will have a current backup on hand in case a device restore becomes necessary. Also, if using OTA update, we recommend plugging your device into a power source for the duration of the download/installation process, so as to prevent the unlikely event of your battery going dead during the update.

en.title: macOS Golden Gate: New Features, Changes, Improvements, and Bugs for Blind and Low Vision Users
en.summary: Apple has today released macOS 27 Golden Gate to the public. As usual, we won’t cover the mainstream features here, concentrating instead on what's new and changed for blind, DeafBlind, and low vision users. For an overview of the mainstream changes, we recommend this in-depth review by MacStories . Please remember to check the section about bugs to see if now is the right time to upgrade. There’s no harm in holding off a few weeks or months to let Apple address a problem you may find too disruptive to deal with. A note to braille users: the AppleVis team members doing testing with macOS Golden Gate are not heavy braille users. We have no information as to how well braille works in this release, so please keep this in mind when upgrading. If you are a braille user who has experience with Golden Gate, please share your findings in the comments to help the community. Changes for VoiceOver and Braille Users Improved Image and Screen Descriptions As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, VoiceOver in macOS Golden Gate can use Apple Intelligence to describe and answer questions about images or the current screen as it appears visually. Focusing on an image and pressing VO-Shift-L will describe the image, and you can find additional options, such as the ability to ask about an image, explore the image spatially, or describe the current screen, by pressing VO-Shift-R from anywhere in macOS. For added convenience, commands in this menu can be mapped in VoiceOver Utility > Commands. Note that while VoiceOver can describe and answer questions about what's on the screen, it cannot directly interact with elements like VOCR or Screen Recognition on iOS and iPadOS can. New Verbosity Options for Coding With macOS Golden Gate, you can customize how information such as line numbers, errors, and warnings are reported by VoiceOver in code editors like Xcode. These settings can be found in the new "Coding" tab in VoiceOver Utility > Verbosity. We do not currently know which code editors besides Xcode respect these settings. New "Actions" rotor for trackpad users With macOS Golden Gate, you can perform custom actions for the focused element, the same actions available in VoiceOver's Actions menu, using trackpad commands. To do this, enable trackpad commands if they're not already enabled, turn the rotor to "Actions," swipe up or down with one finger to select a custom action, and double-tap to activate it. "Ducking Amount" setting The "Ducking Amount" setting for determining how much other audio is ducked when VoiceOver is speaking, originally introduced with iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, has been brought to macOS with the release of Golden Gate. It can be found in VoiceOver Utility > Sound. Braille Improvements While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvements for braille users in macOS Golden Gate: As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, text field labels can now be shown in braille. You can change the format these labels are presented in, or hide them entirely, by going to VoiceOver Utility > Braille > Layout, and clicking Text Field Labels. As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, Braille Access in macOS Golden Gate supports plain text (txt) and portable document format (PDF) files. Improvements for Low Vision Users While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvement for low vision users: As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, content in Accessibility Reader can now be summarized and translated while retaining its original formatting on macOS Golden Gate. If you are a low vision Mac user, we would love to hear in the comments your experience and thoughts on this and any additional enhancements you encounter in macOS Golden Gate. Other Changes As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, the Aaron (English US), Arthur (English UK), Catherine (English Australia), Gordon (English Australia), and Martha (English UK) voices have been reintroduced with macOS Golden Gate. Like other voices, they can be used with Siri, as well as for accessibility functions like VoiceOver and Read & Speak. As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, subtitles for spoken dialog in videos where captioning is not already provided can be generated automatically in macOS Golden Gate. These can be turned on and adjusted when playing a video by clicking the "show legible media selection menu" button in the playback controls group. Writing Tools, previously accessed from many apps' Edit menus, as well as many text fields' context menus, is now accessed with VoiceOver by focusing on a text field and choosing "Show Writing Tools" from the Actions Menu. When toggling Cursor Tracking with VO-F3, its state is reflected in the "Mouse pointer:" popup menu in VoiceOver Utility. In prior versions of macOS, the state of Cursor Tracking was not reflected in this popup menu, which had the potential to confuse users. Change List In its support documentation, Apple lists the following changes for VoiceOver users in macOS Golden Gate: You can now turn off announcements that webpages send automatically, such as live scores, new messages, or status updates. Turn off Enable Web Announcements to silence announcements from a single area of a webpage or from the entire page. VoiceOver remembers your choice for that website, so the area stays silent the next time you visit. With the new Coding tab in the Verbosity category of VoiceOver Utility, you can choose whether VoiceOver announces line numbers, and whether it plays a tone or speaks a description when it encounters an error, a breakpoint, or the program counter. Bug Fixes and New Bugs for VoiceOver Users Below are lists of the bugs we believe to have been resolved in macOS Golden Gate, as well as new bugs introduced in this release. We strongly recommend that you read through the list of new bugs and any replies before updating, as this will allow you to make an informed decision on whether to install macOS Golden Gate or wait for a future release. While we are confident in the status of issues contained in this post, we do not claim that our bug list is definitive or that our assessments are infallible. Some issues may manifest only under specific conditions; this is all the more likely as software continues to add more features, and the number of available configurations and use cases in Apple's ecosystem continues to grow. You likely will not experience every bug that we list, and it is also likely that you will encounter issues that we did not experience during our own testing and daily use of macOS Golden Gate. To ensure the information here is as complete and accurate as possible, we would appreciate input from those who have installed macOS Golden Gate. Please confirm if you are encountering the same problems listed or if you have found workarounds. Please also let us know about any additional issues not mentioned here. Of course, it's even more important that you report any new bugs directly to Apple - they're already aware of the ones listed here. For an explanation of why and how to report bugs to Apple, see this post. Accessibility Bugs Resolved in macOS Golden Gate To the best of our knowledge, Apple does not routinely publish lists of bug fixes for VoiceOver or Braille across releases; thus, it is difficult to get a complete accounting of every issue that has been resolved or what fixes users can expect to see upon upgrading to macOS Golden Gate. With this in mind, our testing suggests that the following issues present in macOS Tahoe have been resolved or meaningfully improved in macOS Golden Gate: VoiceOver no longer speaks list items on webpages unreliably. Pauses between sentences are no longer extended when using VoiceOver's "Say All" command. It is once again possible to reply to a message in the Message app by selecting the "Reply" action in the Actions menu. The Actions menu for Messages in the Messages app no longer contains redundant tapback actions. New Bugs for VoiceOver Users in macOS Golden Gate Our testing suggests that the following bugs have been introduced in macOS Golden Gate: After clicking the “Proofread” button in the Writing Tools popover using VoiceOver, only the Next, Previous, and Close buttons are visible, with no way to view the specific changes made to the text. There is no way to open or redownload apps from the “Apps & Purchases” page in the App Store using VoiceOver, with each app conveyed only as a button with no actions available and nothing to interact with besides the app’s name. To redownload a previously purchased app, you must click the [app name] button to open the product page, and then click the "Redownload" button in the toolbar. The sections and buttons in Safari’s Page Menu lack accessibility labels. Interacting with a section and pressing VO-Space on an item (all of which are clearly labeled) works to activate the item; however, interacting with each item in a section reveals an unlabeled button. When playing audio or video, VoiceOver announces “system has new window” once the media has started playing. The identity and purpose of this window is not clear from this announcement, and no new items appear in the application or window chooser menus. Other Possible Bugs In addition to the bugs listed here, we strongly recommend you read this Megathread about the macOS Golden Gate RC , , as it contains a wealth of community reports about and experiences with the Release Candidate version of the software that may differ from our own. macOS Golden Gate release notes macOS 27 introduces Siri AI powered by Apple Intelligence, new parental controls, and an expansive set of improvements that make your Mac even more responsive, reliable, and delightful. Experience the new Siri AI Introducing Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that’s more personal, more capable, and more conversational. It is integrated into Spotlight, so you can search for answers about almost any topic right from where you already search for things across your system. It can draw on personal context to find things across your messages, mail, photos, and more. And it can get things done across your apps, just by asking. Revisit and resume past conversations in the new dedicated Siri app, synced with iCloud across your Apple devices. Siri AI is rolling out to users, and you can get started by turning it on in Settings. Take action on what’s onscreen With Visual Intelligence, you can select a window of your screen and Siri can answer questions or take action with what’s onscreen, like adding events to your calendar. You can access Visual Intelligence with a dedicated keyboard shortcut — Command-Shift-Space. Powerful new ways to edit photos Use intelligent photo editing tools to reframe a photo after it’s been taken with Spatial Reframing or expand your shot with the Extend tool. And enhancements to Clean Up let you remove distractions with better quality and more realistic infill, even when the scene is complex. New tools to browse in Safari Automatically group your tabs into topics, so related pages are easier to find. With Notify Me, Safari can monitor pages for changes like price drops or restocks and alert you when it’s time to act. Describe an Extension lets you use natural language to create custom extensions, like adding a button to save your favorite recipes. Easily create Shortcuts using natural language With Describe a Shortcut, you can automate daily tasks with a simple description and all of the required steps are assembled on your behalf. For example, you can describe a shortcut to automatically text your partner when you’re headed home from work with an estimated arrival time based on traffic. Even more refined design Updates to Liquid Glass improve readability, and a new slider lets you customize how it looks, from ultra-clear to fully tinted. Uniform toolbars, edge-to-edge sidebars, and more detailed app icons further elevate the design. New child safety features Powerful new parental controls help parents manage what content their children see, who they can communicate with, and when they can access apps. Ask to Browse requires kids to request permission before visiting any new website in Safari. Communication Safety expands its protections to help keep conversations safe. Time Allowances gives parents more flexible ways to manage kids’ time in apps across categories. Schedules manage which apps kids can access at different times of day and throughout the week. A more responsive and delightful experience An expansive set of improvements make your Mac even faster, more reliable, and easier to use. Better search in Spotlight and Mail helps you find what you’re looking for with greater ease. AirDrop Transfers and network file browsing happen faster. And many more improvements make your day-to-day use more enjoyable. Learn more Discover even more powerful capabilities in the next release by visiting apple.com/os/macos . For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: support.apple.com/100100 . Some features may not be available in all regions or on all Apple devices. To learn more, please visit: apple.com/macos/feature-availability . Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: apple.com/apple-intelligence . Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and battery life. To learn more, please visit: support.apple.com/125039 . In Conclusion We would like to thank everyone in our community who contributed to AppleVis' testing and bug-reporting efforts during the macOS Golden Gate beta cycle - be it through our Community Bug Program or just by posting on our Forum. Our information about this release is more complete because of you, and we are very grateful to all who took the time to contribute. We'd love to hear your thoughts after you've had a chance to install the upgrade. What new features do you find most useful? Are there any changes you don't like? Please share your feedback in the comments below. When doing so, we ask that you please keep the discussion focused on accessibility issues specifically introduced or fixed in macOS Golden Gate. Our release posts tend to be widely read and garner many helpful responses, so it is all the more important that readers can easily find relevant information. Also, please remember that upgrade decisions are personal, with each user's situation unique - there is no right or wrong choice. Comments criticizing others' decisions are not constructive and do nothing to add to the discussion; but they do set a negative tone and get in the way of readers finding helpful information. Furthermore, not experiencing an issue yourself does not mean that it doesn't exist for others, as bugs can be configuration-specific. Stating that an issue doesn't exist simply because you haven't encountered it is unhelpful. Our aim with these posts is to provide a forum for respectful, constructive, and honest sharing of experiences that inform decisions and empower people. In closing, we thank Apple's Accessibility team for their prompt response in fixing many of the bugs reported during the macOS Golden Gate beta cycle. However, many longstanding issues remain unresolved, and we find the inability to fully use the Proofread function, a key feature of Apple Intelligence, during a cycle where enhancements to Apple Intelligence were heavily emphasized, incredibly disappointing. We encourage Apple to promptly address this and other outstanding accessibility issues discussed in this post and the comments below so that macOS can be as accessible, usable, and enjoyable as possible for all users. To install macOS Golden Gate, choose System Settings from the Apple menu, select General in the table, click Software Update in the scroll area, and click the Upgrade Now button to begin the upgrade process. If other updates are available, you can click the Info button to see details about them and select specific updates to install. More information on how to update the software on your Mac is available on this Apple Support page.

Apple has today released macOS 27 Golden Gate to the public. As usual, we won’t cover the mainstream features here, concentrating instead on what's new and changed for blind, DeafBlind, and low vision users. For an overview of the mainstream changes, we recommend this in-depth review by MacStories .

Please remember to check the section about bugs to see if now is the right time to upgrade. There’s no harm in holding off a few weeks or months to let Apple address a problem you may find too disruptive to deal with.

A note to braille users: the AppleVis team members doing testing with macOS Golden Gate are not heavy braille users. We have no information as to how well braille works in this release, so please keep this in mind when upgrading. If you are a braille user who has experience with Golden Gate, please share your findings in the comments to help the community.

As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, VoiceOver in macOS Golden Gate can use Apple Intelligence to describe and answer questions about images or the current screen as it appears visually. Focusing on an image and pressing VO-Shift-L will describe the image, and you can find additional options, such as the ability to ask about an image, explore the image spatially, or describe the current screen, by pressing VO-Shift-R from anywhere in macOS. For added convenience, commands in this menu can be mapped in VoiceOver Utility > Commands. Note that while VoiceOver can describe and answer questions about what's on the screen, it cannot directly interact with elements like VOCR or Screen Recognition on iOS and iPadOS can.

With macOS Golden Gate, you can customize how information such as line numbers, errors, and warnings are reported by VoiceOver in code editors like Xcode. These settings can be found in the new "Coding" tab in VoiceOver Utility > Verbosity. We do not currently know which code editors besides Xcode respect these settings.

With macOS Golden Gate, you can perform custom actions for the focused element, the same actions available in VoiceOver's Actions menu, using trackpad commands. To do this, enable trackpad commands if they're not already enabled, turn the rotor to "Actions," swipe up or down with one finger to select a custom action, and double-tap to activate it.

The "Ducking Amount" setting for determining how much other audio is ducked when VoiceOver is speaking, originally introduced with iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, has been brought to macOS with the release of Golden Gate. It can be found in VoiceOver Utility > Sound.

While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvements for braille users in macOS Golden Gate:

While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvement for low vision users:

If you are a low vision Mac user, we would love to hear in the comments your experience and thoughts on this and any additional enhancements you encounter in macOS Golden Gate.

macOS 27 introduces Siri AI powered by Apple Intelligence, new parental controls, and an expansive set of improvements that make your Mac even more responsive, reliable, and delightful.

Experience the new Siri AI

Introducing Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that’s more personal, more capable, and more conversational. It is integrated into Spotlight, so you can search for answers about almost any topic right from where you already search for things across your system. It can draw on personal context to find things across your messages, mail, photos, and more. And it can get things done across your apps, just by asking. Revisit and resume past conversations in the new dedicated Siri app, synced with iCloud across your Apple devices. Siri AI is rolling out to users, and you can get started by turning it on in Settings.

Take action on what’s onscreen

With Visual Intelligence, you can select a window of your screen and Siri can answer questions or take action with what’s onscreen, like adding events to your calendar. You can access Visual Intelligence with a dedicated keyboard shortcut — Command-Shift-Space.

Use intelligent photo editing tools to reframe a photo after it’s been taken with Spatial Reframing or expand your shot with the Extend tool. And enhancements to Clean Up let you remove distractions with better quality and more realistic infill, even when the scene is complex.

Automatically group your tabs into topics, so related pages are easier to find. With Notify Me, Safari can monitor pages for changes like price drops or restocks and alert you when it’s time to act. Describe an Extension lets you use natural language to create custom extensions, like adding a button to save your favorite recipes.

With Describe a Shortcut, you can automate daily tasks with a simple description and all of the required steps are assembled on your behalf. For example, you can describe a shortcut to automatically text your partner when you’re headed home from work with an estimated arrival time based on traffic.

Powerful new parental controls help parents manage what content their children see, who they can communicate with, and when they can access apps. Time Allowances gives parents more flexible ways to manage kids’ time in apps across categories. Schedules manage which apps kids can access at different times of day and throughout the week.

An expansive set of improvements make your Mac even faster, more reliable, and easier to use. Better search in Spotlight and Mail helps you find what you’re looking for with greater ease. AirDrop Transfers and network file browsing happen faster. And many more improvements make your day-to-day use more enjoyable.

en.body:
Published 14 September 2026 by Aleksandar Đurić

NetBoard turns your computer into an instant input device for your phone, allowing you to type quickly, accurately, and effortlessly using your computer’s full physical keyboard.

Built from the ground up with accessibility (A11y) as a core value, NetBoard is designed for blind, visually impaired, and motor-impaired users who find mobile touchscreen keyboards challenging to use with screen readers such as TalkBack.

Windows app: Download NetBoard for Windows .

NetBoard does not collect, log, or store your keystrokes, clipboard history, or audio files. Data is encrypted and processed strictly in transit. The app contains no ads and has no hidden fees.

Free or paid:

The app is fully accessible because it was developed by a blind programmer.

es.title: Ya disponible la segunda beta de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 2 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la segunda beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la segunda beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 2 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 2 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es d26386e7ac3ac6d245c8adcfc82c07e9332278360af3396b69888b6b31e08d33. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la segunda beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: Blind Accessibility Keyboard (BAK)
en.summary: Blind Accessibility Keyboard (BAK) is an Android keyboard for blind and low-vision users. Refined over many years together with blind users, it was rebuilt from…
en.body:
Published 13 September 2026 by Philip Heyse

Blind Accessibility Keyboard (BAK) is an Android keyboard for blind and low-vision users. Refined over many years together with blind users, it was rebuilt from the ground up in summer 2026: modern, faster, and adjustable in great detail.

Two ways to type, both letting you check a key before it is sent:

– Lift to Type: slide your finger over the keys, hear each one, and commit by lifting it – Double Tap to Type: the first tap reads the key, a second tap confirms it

1. Setup and settings:

Setup is guided step by step and confirms out loud when the keyboard is enabled and selected.

The settings screen is made for TalkBack: a switch and its label are read as one element, and sections announced with a “Section:” prefix.

Settings can be saved to a file and restored later. A session log can be exported or e-mailed if you need help.

2. Keyboard layouts:

264 layouts are included. For most languages you can choose between Simple (four rows), Fluent Flow (five rows with numbers), Fluent Flow with Cursor (plus cursor keys), PC (Ctrl, Alt and function keys), PC with Num Pad, and Robo Gear (familiar from standard smartphone keyboards).

Hold the space bar for the Quick Menu to switch layouts. The full list of languages is at the end of this text.

The app itself is translated into 30 languages, including Finnish, Malay and Urdu.

3. What you hear:

– Adjustable speed and pitch, with upper and lower case told apart by pitch – Choice of speech engine, with language, country and voice – Optional NATO alphabet, so “B” and “D” are never confused – Spoken names for punctuation, symbols and emoji – Announcements when the keyboard opens or closes, when you move between letters, numbers, symbols and emoji, and on Shift, Alt or Ctrl changes – Key click sounds in three styles, with adjustable volume – Vibration when typing and on gestures, each switchable separately

4. Voice input:

Start dictation with the microphone key or the Quick Menu, and choose between:

– Your device’s own dictation – A model running on your device: no account needed, works offline, though less accurate than the online options – Popular AI services, using your own API key, stored encrypted on your device only

5. Typing support:

– Auto-correct for many of the supported languages. One Backspace restores the original word. Never runs in password fields. – Text shortcuts: “brt” becomes “Best regards, Tom”. One Backspace undoes it. – Clipboard history above the keys. Tap an entry to insert it. – Your own keys for text you often need, such as your e-mail address – Optional capital letter at the start of a sentence – Adjustable delay and repeat speed when holding Delete or Backspace

6. Subscription:

BAK is funded by a small subscription. It costs less than the equivalent of one US dollar per month, and follows the local price level, so in many countries it is lower. It pays for ongoing work: fixing bugs, keeping up with new Android versions, and adding features. Before subscribing, you can try the keyboard in the test field on the app’s home screen. A subscription is needed to use it in other apps.

7. Help and contact: – https://bright-side.de/bak/ – ba * @ ********* de.de

The Help section in the app has the documentation, the mailing list, and a way to e-mail the developer.

8. Layouts for your language:

Arabic (also with French), Belarusian, Bengali, Bulgarian (Cyrillic, Latin, Phonetic), Canadian (also French, Multilingual), Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English (UK, USA), French (France, Switzerland), German (Germany, Switzerland), Greek, Gujarati, Hebrew, Hindi (also InScript), Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian (Italy, Switzerland), Kannada, Marathi, Norwegian, Persian, Polish (also programmer), Portuguese (also Brazilian ABNT), Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Spanish (Spain, Latin America), Swedish, Tamil, Telugu, Turkish (F and Q), Ukrainian, Vietnamese.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

The keyboard app was specifically designed for blind or visually impaired users.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

en.body:
Published 10 September 2026 by HushBook

HushBook is an audiobook read-along app built for readers with ADHD, dyslexia, or poor reading comprehension. It plays the audiobook files you already own and highlights every word in sync with the narration, so the eye and ear stay locked together. Fully on-device: offline, no account, no ads, free on Android and iOS, with about 20,000 public-domain titles included.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

The core accessibility feature is word-by-word highlighting synced to the narrator's voice, designed for readers who struggle to follow text alone or audio alone. Everything works offline with no account required. Screen-reader testing is ongoing and we welcome feedback from blind and low-vision users at hello@hushbook.app.

es.title: Accesibilidad y Tecnología Vive el fútbol accesible con Movistar Touch en el estadio Riyadh Air Metropolitano.
es.summary: Gracias a la colaboración entre la ONCE, Movistar y el Atlético de Madrid, las personas afiliadas podrán disfrutar de una experiencia más accesible e inmersiva durante los partidos de fútbol que se celebren en el estadio Riyadh Air Metropolitano.
es.body:
Gracias a la colaboración entre la ONCE, Movistar y el Atlético de Madrid, las personas afiliadas podrán disfrutar de una experiencia más accesible e inmersiva durante los partidos de fútbol que se celebren en el estadio Riyadh Air Metropolitano.

Se trata de Movistar Touch , un servicio gratuito dirigido a aficionados con entrada para el encuentro, que permite seguir el desarrollo del partido mediante audiodescripción y una tableta háptica capaz de reproducir en tiempo real la posición del balón sobre el terreno de juego. Esta tecnología ofrece una nueva forma de vivir la emoción del fútbol y constituye un excelente ejemplo de cómo la innovación puede contribuir a derribar barreras y favorecer la participación de todas las personas.

Actualmente, el Riyadh Air Metropolitano es el único estadio de España que ofrece este sistema. Las personas afiliadas interesadas en utilizarlo deberán solicitarlo previamente enviando un correo electrónico a inclusion@atleticodemadrid.com , indicando el partido de LALIGA para el que desean adquirir entradas y hacer uso del servicio.

Es importante tener en cuenta que Movistar Touch dispone de un número limitado de unidades, por lo que se recomienda realizar la solicitud con la mayor antelación posible.

Esta iniciativa se enmarca en la colaboración que el Atlético de Madrid mantiene desde hace años con la ONCE y Fundación ONCE para seguir mejorando la accesibilidad de sus instalaciones y servicios, reforzando así su compromiso con un deporte más inclusivo y accesible para todos.

en.title: Issue Affecting Some JAWS and Fusion Features Now Resolved
en.summary: The issue we reported on September 4 has been resolved with no action needed on your part. Last week a Microsoft update changed the way accessibility support is enabled for applications that use certain Microsoft web technologies. As a result, JAWS was not always receiving the information it needed from those applications, and some features …
en.body:
The issue we reported on September 4 has been resolved with no action needed on your part.

Last week a Microsoft update changed the way accessibility support is enabled for applications that use certain Microsoft web technologies. As a result, JAWS was not always receiving the information it needed from those applications, and some features provided no speech or braille. This affected the JAWS Results Viewer, OCR Viewer, Picture Smart, and Message Center, along with New Outlook and Microsoft Copilot 365.

On September 6 we deployed a temporary change to JAWS so that customers would not have to wait while the underlying problem was still being investigated. On September 7 Microsoft released an update that corrected the root cause. Because that update resolves the problem at its source, we have since removed our temporary change.

The Microsoft update is delivered automatically, so there is nothing for you to install or turn on. The temporary work-around we shared last week, toggling the Touch Cursor off and on, is no longer needed.

If you are still experiencing the problem, please restart your computer so the Microsoft update can take effect. If that does not resolve it, please contact your local dealer or our technical support team.

We appreciate everyone who reported this to us and who let us know when things began working again. Those reports helped us confirm the cause quickly and gave us what we needed to work with Microsoft toward a resolution.

en.title: In-Process 8th September 2026
en.summary: It’s a busy and exciting time – it’s release time! Let’s dive in and see what’s new: NVDA 2026.2 Magnifier A new Beta already? Resetting to Factory Defaults NVDA 2026.2 NVDA 2026.2 has been released! This release includes a new built-in Magnifier feature, improvements to touch gestures and navigation, and expanded speech and braille capabilities.… Read More
en.body:
It’s a busy and exciting time – it’s release time! Let’s dive in and see what’s new:

NVDA 2026.2 has been released ! This release includes a new built-in Magnifier feature, improvements to touch gestures and navigation, and expanded speech and braille capabilities.

The Magnifier provides zoom and color filtering options to assist users with visual impairments. The Magnifier currently only supports full screen mode, with docked modes planned in a future release. Touch support has been significantly expanded with new pinch gestures and touch-based browse mode navigation for web content. You can now navigate between links, headings, form fields, and other elements using touch flicks.

Speech features have been enhanced with support for custom speech dictionaries that can be provided by add-ons and new dictionary entry types for more granular control. A new voice setting for OneCore voices was added to control pauses after punctuation. A new command allows repeating the last spoken information, with the ability to display it in a browsable message. The default gesture to repeat the last spoken information is NVDA+x , which can be changed in the Input Gestures dialog.

The braille display can now automatically scroll, and DotPad devices support multi-button combinations. The default gesture to toggle automatic scroll is NVDA+alt+k .

Liblouis has been updated with new Italian and Estonian braille tables. When resetting NVDA to factory defaults, an Undo button is now available to restore the previous configuration.

Download the new version from the NVDA 2026.2 release post (or by checking for updates from within NVDA).

As well as the article below, and a new extensive section on the magnifier in the User Guide, our “Basic Training for NVDA” module has been updated with a number of updates. Of particular interest is a new section on the magnifier, there is also a topic covering reading the last spoken information and other new and improved content. These new updates are currently only available in the electronic text version. You can purchase Basic Training for NVDA from our shop . If you have already purchased the module, you can download the new version with the Magnifier section from the downloads page after logging into your NV Access account .

We are very excited to incorporate a magnifier into NVDA for the first time. We have had a lot of comments from users who are excited for this feature, and we’ve had some questions too, so let’s cover off some of the things it can and cannot do, and why it is a useful addition to NVDA:

First Release Firstly, it’s worth highlighting that this is the first release of NVDA with a magnifier and so the features will improve over time. We try to ship NVDA features incrementally, keeping the initial design scope small and allowing for early user feedback. This allows us to grow the magnifier in response to user reaction. Currently NVDA only works as a full-screen magnifier. We plan to extend the options in future releases. Adding windowed / docked modes is a high priority once bugs are addressed and the full-screen mode is more polished.

What CAN the magnifier do? The magnifier has most of the features you might expect from such a feature: You can zoom in and out (from 1x up to 50x) The view will follow the mouse, keyboard focus, browse mode focus and NVDA navigator object and review cursor – user selectable You can pan the view with the keyboard, in configurable increments, or jump to the edges of the screen You can adjust the colours (normal, inverted or greyscale) You can choose how objects are tracked (Centred or relative to their position on screen) You can configure the keystrokes for the various functions There is a keystroke to briefly zoom out and show an overview of the screen

We have made a short demo of the magnification feature on our YouTube channel .

Should I change magnifiers? Particularly if you currently use another magnification solution, we very much encourage you to try out the NVDA magnifier. We are interested in your feedback, and particularly where you would like to see our feature improve.

If you already use Windows magnifier or another program, you can keep using it and it will continue to work with NVDA’s speech functions. Just as we don’t recommend having two screen readers running at once, we also wouldn’t recommend having NVDA’s magnifier AND another magnifier running at the same time.

If you do currently use Windows Magnifier, some of the reasons you may consider NVDA’s magnifier: It starts when NVDA starts (once you enable it) Configurable keystrokes Greyscale colour filtering mode Relative tracking mode Ability to follow NVDA’s object navigation and review cursor Keys to jump to edges of screen No settings window always on screen Ability to set your desired settings once and save to a portable copy you can use on any computer

If you use Windows magnifier in docked or lens mode, or some of the other features which haven’t yet made it into the NVDA magnifier in NVDA 2026.2, then you may wish to stay with Windows magnifier for now – but we do encourage you to try out the NVDA magnifier and let us know what you think.

Before we even got this edition of In-Process finished, to tell you all about 2026.2…. we ALREADY have a new beta? Of NVDA 2026.3 ? Yep! And I’m not going to talk about that yet – if you want to check it out, please head to the beta release announcement . What I did want to briefly mention, was how we came to have a new beta out, when the paint isn’t even dry on NVDA 2026.2?

Great question! And it comes down to how we develop software. Both our internal developers, and the community are constantly working on improving features, fixing bugs, and adding new things into NVDA. As a new piece of code gets incorporated into NVDA, it goes into an “Alpha” build – an early pre-release build with whatever has been changed recently. This lets our developers and our most dedicated testers try it out and give feedback. These come out almost daily (and sometimes several in one day). Because of the quick turnaround, we don’t share them on social media or here on the blog, but if you’d like to try them out, alpha builds are publicly available from the snapshots page . Be aware that they may not be as polished as the stable releases – though the process to test them out is identical.

So, generally a week after a stable release, we collate all the things which have been in alpha for at least a couple of weeks, and put them together into a “beta” release of the next version. While we may still have some features we are working on for later betas, as well any regressions or major issues discovered from the previous release, we can turn much of our development attention on towards the NEXT release.

So, if you ever find an issue with NVDA, the sooner you let us know, the sooner we can prioritise it and work on a fix as needed.

One of the perhaps less glamourous updates in NVDA 2026.2 is to a feature you hopefully don’t ever need to use.

“When resetting NVDA to factory defaults, an Undo button is now available to restore the previous configuration”

We’ve covered resetting NVDA to factory defaults previously , though it is worth being aware of. While something you hopefully don’t need, if you ever DO need it, it’s good to know it exists. With this new change, if you reset NVDA to factory defaults, a dialog appears advising “Your configuration has been reset to factory defaults. Choose OK to keep factory defaults, or Undo to restore your previous configuration”. This could be useful just in case you ever inadvertently activate the wrong item on the NVDA menu for instance, and may hopefully save you from needing go through setting up NVDA to your preferences again.

That’s all for this week, do update to NVDA 2026.2 if you haven’t already, and we’d love to hear your feedback on the new features – the magnifier of course, but also the other updates.

Contera giratoria con cáncamo para bastones Asturias 2

Una historia entrañable con la que ayudar a tu peque a detectar y comunicar mejor sus sentimientos.

es.summary: Normal 0 false 21 false false false ES X-NONE X-NONE /* Style Definitions */ table.MsoNormalTable {mso-style-name:"Tabla normal"; mso-tstyle-rowband-size:0; mso-tstyle-colband-size:0; mso-style-noshow:yes; mso-style-priority:99; mso-style-parent:""; mso-padding-alt:0cm 5.4pt 0cm 5.4pt; mso-para-margin-top:0cm; mso-para-margin-right:0cm; mso-para-margin-bottom:8.0pt; mso-para-margin-left:0cm; line-height:107%; mso-pagination:widow-orphan; font-size:11.0pt; font-family:"Calibri",sans-serif; mso-ascii-font-family:Calibri; mso-ascii-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-hansi-font-family:Calibri; mso-hansi-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family:"Times New Roman"; mso-bidi-theme-font:minor-bidi; mso-fareast-language:EN-US;} Hola gente, ¿qué tal les va? Muy atentos: Después de casi dos años de desarrollo, por fin llega TCA ConvertDoc 1.5. No es una simple actualización: es un salto generacional con las funcionalidades que me habéis ido pidiendo en los comentarios del blog, sobre todo desde la entrada de la versión 1.4. Para quienes aún no lo conozcan: ¿Qué es TCA ConvertDoc? TCA ConvertDoc es una pequeña utilidad portable y gratuita para Windows, con interfaz 100% accesible y atajos de teclado, que nos permite convertir entre multitud de formatos de documentos (doc, docx, RTF, epub, pdf, HTML, odt, txt, markdown, PNG, JPG, PPTx), hacer OCR a imágenes y PDFs, y ahora, además, traducir. Y todo, de forma individual o por lotes (carpeta entera de una sola vez). Pues bien, la 1.5 llega cargada de novedades. Os las cuento todas. Novedades de TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 1. Conversión DOCX → PDF (individual y por lotes) Ahora podéis convertir documentos de Word a PDF con un solo clic. ¿Tenéis una carpeta llena de? docx? La conversión masiva procesa todo el directorio de golpe, manteniendo el formato, las imágenes y la estructura del documento. Perfecto para preparar entregas, archivar o compartir. 2. Conversión PPTX → Markdown (individual y por lotes) Algunos me preguntasteis en la entrada de la 1.4 por qué ciertas presentaciones de PowerPoint no se pueden leer con lectores de pantalla. Pues esta es una de las soluciones: extrae el contenido de tus presentaciones a Markdown limpio y editable, ideal para documentación, blogs, wikis o migrar contenido. También funciona en lote para carpetas completas. 3. PDF escaneado PDF buscable (OCR) "¿Se puede convertir un pdf en un pdf con capacidad de búsqueda?" — me preguntasteis en los comentarios de la 1.4. ¡Ahora sí! Añades un PDF que es solo imagen (un escaneo sin capa de texto), TCA ConvertDoc le aplica OCR y te devuelve un PDF con texto seleccionable y buscable. Accesibilidad real para documentos heredados, del tipo que sea. 4. JPG / PNG PDF buscable Construye PDFs accesibles a partir de imágenes sueltas. Cada imagen pasa por OCR y se une en un único PDF donde puedes buscar, copiar y seleccionar el texto. Ideal para digitalizar notas, facturas, páginas de libros o documentos fotografiados con el móvil. 5. Traducción integrada! (¡la gran novedad!) Llevaba muchísimo tiempo queriendo incorporarle la traducción a TCA ConvertDoc, y por fin está aquí. Ahora el programa es capaz de traducir archivos completos a cualquier idioma usando dos motores: • Argos Translate | Offline | Descarga previa de los paquetes de idioma (privacidad total, sin internet) • Google Translate | Online | Conexión a internet, máxima calidad Formatos soportados: .txt, .docx y .pdf. Y lo mejor de todo: traduce incluso archivos grandes como libros enteros. El motor procesa el texto en fragmentos inteligentes, mantiene la estructura del documento (párrafos, saltos de página, estilos en DOCX) y te entrega el archivo traducido listo para usar. Nada de copiar y pegar por trozos, ni de chocar con límites ridículos de caracteres. Un detalle importante sobre Argos: la primera vez que uses Argos con un idioma, te aparecerá un diálogo ofreciéndote descargar los paquetes de ese idioma... y solo esa única vez. A partir de ahí, ese idioma queda instalado en el programa y funciona totalmente sin conexión. Tranquilo, no te lo volverá a pedir. 6. Selector de idiomas del OCR (Tesseract) completo En la 1.4 teníamos 3 idiomas de OCR (español, inglés e italiano). Ahora, en el cuadro combinado de idioma del OCR aparecen todos los idiomas que soporta Tesseract. Ya no hay que editar configs a mano ni adivinar códigos: eliges el idioma y listo. 7. Arreglos y optimizaciones internas OCR de archivos grandes: se ha reescrito el proceso para manejar PDFs e imágenes de gran tamaño sin agotar la memoria ni bloquear la interfaz. Gestión de hilos optimizada en las conversiones por lotes. Mejor detección de orientación y enderezado automático en imágenes escaneadas. Logs más claros y barra de progreso real en las operaciones largas. Y muchas otras mejoras internas que hacen el programa más estable y rápido. Requisitos para utilizar TCA ConvertDoc 1.5: • Windows10 (x64) en adelante. • portable, sin instalación. • Para Argos: el programa te ofrece descargar los paquetes del idioma la primera vez que lo uses (un solo diálogo), y luego funciona offline • Para Google Translate: conexión a internet Tip: si vas a trabajar mucho con traducción offline, entra a Argos, descarga de una vez los idiomas que más uses (español, inglés, francés, alemán, chino, japonés, árabe...) y olvídate. Luego todo irá 100% sin conexión. Tutorial: 📘 TCA ConvertDoc 1.5: OCR en PDF, 🚀 traduce libros y más! En este tutorial les mostraré: • Les mostraré la nueva conversión de Docx a PDF. • Conversión de PPTX a Markdown. • Conversión de un PDF (que son imágenes) a un PDF accesible (que admite búsqueda). • Construir un archivo PDF a partir de imágenes Jpg o PNG. • Muestra de que todos los idiomas ahora se cargan en el Motor OCR Tesseract. • Como traducir un documento en formato TXT a otro idioma de forma Online usando Google Translate (• conversión del inglés al español). • Como traducir un documento en formato Docx, utilizando la traducción OfLine con Argos Translate (• muestra del inglés al francés, descarga de idiomas y más). • Finalmente les mostraré, como traducir un PDF a otro idioma. La descarga. Les dejaré en la descarga: • El audio tutorial (en los canales Odysse y YouTube estará en video tutorial). • El programa TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 x64. • Archivo con las librerías visual estudio C++. Espero les sea de mucha utilidad: Dos años son mucho tiempo en software, pero TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 llega para quedarse. No es un parche: es un salto que cubre el ciclo completo —convertir, OCR, buscar, traducir— en una sola herramienta accesible, portable, gratuita y sin suscripciones. Si trabajas con documentos, investigas, digitalizas archivo o necesitas mover contenido entre idiomas, esta versión te va a ahorrar horas. Y la traducción de libros enteros, esa que tanto esperabais, por fin es una realidad. ¿Qué funcionalidad echabas más en falta? ¿Se te ocurre algo para la 1?6? Y ya sabes, Si te gusta este contenido, Apóyanos haciendo una donación: Dona aquí en PayPal. compártelo en: Facebook, X. Deja un comentario sobre esta entrada. Síguenos en X: Abajo tienes el botón. Suscríbete al blog: Ahora puedes unirte a nuestros grupos de WhatsApp o Telegram: Puedes escribir al mail del blog con tus datos si deseas ingresar a los mismos. Escucha todos nuestros audio tutoriales, cómodamente: Entrando desde aquí, a nuestro canal en YouTube. Ahora también, en nuestro canal en Odysse: Entra al canal de Tecnoconocimiento Accesible en Odysse. O si prefieres escúchanos en: Anchor: Escúchanos en Anchor. Ponte en contacto con nosotros, déjanos tus sugerencias, dudas, o comentarios, abajo tienes un sencillo formulario, o si lo prefieres, escríbenos al correo del blog: tecnoconocimientoaccesible@gmail.com Los aportes siempre serán bienvenidos. cuando nos escribas por uno de los medios con alguna sugerencia, se publicará con tu nombre. además, como ya se sabe, puedes publicar esta entrada en otro sitio, pero no te olvides citar la fuente. El motor procesa el texto en fragmentos inteligentes, mantiene la estructura del documento (párrafos, saltos de página, estilos en DOCX) y te entrega el archivo traducido listo para usar. Nada de copiar y pegar por trozos, ni de chocar con límites ridículos de caracteres.

Un detalle importante sobre Argos: la primera vez que uses Argos con un idioma, te aparecerá un diálogo ofreciéndote descargar los paquetes de ese idioma... y solo esa única vez. A partir de ahí, ese idioma queda instalado en el programa y funciona totalmente sin conexión. Tranquilo, no te lo volverá a pedir.

En la 1.4 teníamos 3 idiomas de OCR (español, inglés e italiano). Ahora, en el cuadro combinado de idioma del OCR aparecen todos los idiomas que soporta Tesseract. Ya no hay que editar configs a mano ni adivinar códigos: eliges el idioma y listo.

OCR de archivos grandes: se ha reescrito el proceso para manejar PDFs e imágenes de gran tamaño sin agotar la memoria ni bloquear la interfaz.

Gestión de hilos optimizada en las conversiones por lotes.

Mejor detección de orientación y enderezado automático en imágenes escaneadas.

Logs más claros y barra de progreso real en las operaciones largas.

Y muchas otras mejoras internas que hacen el programa más estable y rápido.

• Windows10 (x64) en adelante.

• portable, sin instalación.

• Para Argos: el programa te ofrece descargar los paquetes del idioma la primera vez que lo uses (un solo diálogo), y luego funciona offline

• Para Google Translate: conexión a internet

Tip: si vas a trabajar mucho con traducción offline, entra a Argos, descarga de una vez los idiomas que más uses (español, inglés, francés, alemán, chino, japonés, árabe...) y olvídate. Luego todo irá 100% sin conexión.

En este tutorial les mostraré:

• Les mostraré la nueva conversión de Docx a PDF.

• Conversión de PPTX a Markdown.

• Conversión de un PDF (que son imágenes) a un PDF accesible (que admite búsqueda).

• Construir un archivo PDF a partir de imágenes Jpg o PNG.

• Muestra de que todos los idiomas ahora se cargan en el Motor OCR Tesseract.

• Como traducir un documento en formato TXT a otro idioma de forma Online usando Google Translate (• conversión del inglés al español).

• Como traducir un documento en formato Docx, utilizando la traducción OfLine con Argos Translate (• muestra del inglés al francés, descarga de idiomas y más).

• Finalmente les mostraré, como traducir un PDF a otro idioma.

Les dejaré en la descarga:

• El audio tutorial (en los canales Odysse y YouTube estará en video tutorial).

• El programa TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 x64.

• Archivo con las librerías visual estudio C++.

Espero les sea de mucha utilidad:

Dos años son mucho tiempo en software, pero TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 llega para quedarse. No es un parche: es un salto que cubre el ciclo completo —convertir, OCR, buscar, traducir— en una sola herramienta accesible, portable, gratuita y sin suscripciones.

Si trabajas con documentos, investigas, digitalizas archivo o necesitas mover contenido entre idiomas, esta versión te va a ahorrar horas. Y la traducción de libros enteros, esa que tanto esperabais, por fin es una realidad.

es.title: Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 1 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 1 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 1 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 288e684536edb011710d760fc18ba7b652241085742e304e17d8ee01ede2d20f. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

es.summary: ¡Hola, comunidad! ¿Cómo han ido estos meses de descanso? Esperamos que hayan servido para cargar las pilas y empezar este nuevo año lectivo con energía. Nosotros, aunque no hemos desconectado del todo para informarte de la llegada de NVDA 2026.2 y actualizar traducciones, estamos listos para seguir adelante con nuestra actividad habitual. Si recuerdas el … Continuar leyendo "Regresan las voces Tiflotecnia a la tienda de NVDA en español" La entrada Regresan las voces Tiflotecnia a la tienda de NVDA en español se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
¡Hola, comunidad! ¿Cómo han ido estos meses de descanso? Esperamos que hayan servido para cargar las pilas y empezar este nuevo año lectivo con energía. Nosotros, aunque no hemos desconectado del todo para informarte de la llegada de NVDA 2026.2 y actualizar traducciones, estamos listos para seguir adelante con nuestra actividad habitual. Si recuerdas el anuncio de la beta 7 de NVDA 2026.2 , vino acompañado de una mala noticia: el fallecimiento de Rui Fontes, miembro muy activo de la comunidad a nivel internacional y propietario de Tiflotecnia, la compañía que actualmente comercializa las voces más recientes de Vocalizer para NVDA. Tras este triste anuncio, la venta de las voces quedó en pausa, a la espera de que se aclarase la situación en Tiflotecnia. Desde NVDA.es nos complace anunciar que dicha aclaración ya ha tenido lugar, y por tanto volvemos a reactivar la venta de este sintetizador de voz rápido y de alta calidad. En consecuencia, ya puedes volver a adquirir licencias completas por 90 euros, y actualizaciones de licencias de la versión 3 a la 4 por 50 euros, en ambos casos con impuestos incluidos. Recuerda que cada licencia te permitirá usar el sintetizador en hasta tres equipos de forma simultánea. Si vas a formatear o quieres hacer cambios relevantes de hardware, puedes devolver tu licencia al servidor para recuperarla más adelante. Además, es posible activar y desactivar licencias en equipos que no disponen de conexión a Internet, algo que con la versión 3.0 no se podía hacer. Y por si fuera poco, una sola licencia incluye todas las voces disponibles, ¡en todos los idiomas y con todas las calidades! Si todavía no lo has hecho, puedes instalar y probar estas voces sin coste alguno durante una semana. Te animamos a hacerlo, ¡la experiencia merece la pena! ¡Hasta la próxima!

La entrada Regresan las voces Tiflotecnia a la tienda de NVDA en español se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

blindGram is an independent accessible Telegram client for blind and low-vision Android users, based on Telegram’s open-source Android code.

Its optional blindGram Assistant reads text inside images, provides offline image labels, and converts voice messages and round videos to text offline in 23 languages without Telegram Premium.

Optional AI features provide detailed image descriptions, summaries, follow-up questions, and questions about any message through the user’s own OpenRouter, OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or compatible provider. AI features remain off until enabled.

Website: https://en.blindgram.ir/

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Designed specifically for blind and low-vision users . Interface and message actions are optimized for screen-reader navigation, with primary testing using TalkBack .

Assistant results open in accessible dialogs or conversation screens where text can be read, selected, and copied.

Offline OCR , image labels, and voice-to-text require no account or Telegram Premium.

AI features are optional and clearly disclose when content leaves the device.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

BlindGram 15.0; Supports Android 5.0 and newer;
