es.title: Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.2
es.summary: Tras 11 versiones beta y 2 candidatas a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.2, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.2" La entrada Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tras 11 versiones beta y 2 candidatas a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.2, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye una nueva función de magnificador integrado, mejoras en los gestos táctiles y la navegación, y una ampliación de funciones de voz y braille. El magnificador ofrece opciones de aumentos y de filtrado de colores para ayudar a los usuarios con discapacidad visual. Actualmente, el Magnificador solo es compatible con el modo a pantalla completa, aunque en una futura actualización se prevé la incorporación de modos acoplados. Se ha ampliado considerablemente la compatibilidad táctil con nuevos gestos de pellizco y la navegación por el contenido web mediante el modo táctil. Ahora puedes desplazarte entre enlaces, encabezados, campos de formulario y otros elementos mediante gestos táctiles. Se han mejorado las funciones de voz con la compatibilidad con diccionarios de voz personalizados que pueden proporcionarse mediante complementos, así como con nuevos tipos de entradas de diccionario que permiten un control más preciso. Se ha añadido una nueva configuración de voz para las voces de OneCore con el fin de controlar las pausas tras los signos de puntuación. Una nueva orden permite repetir la última información verbalizada, con la posibilidad de mostrarla en un mensaje que se pueda leer. El gesto predeterminado para repetir la última información leída en voz alta es NVDA+x, que se puede modificar en el cuadro de diálogo «Gestos de entrada». Ahora, la pantalla braille puede desplazarse automáticamente y los dispositivos DotPad admiten combinaciones de varios botones. El atajo predeterminado para activar o desactivar el desplazamiento automático es NVDA+Alt+k. Liblouis se ha actualizado con nuevas tablas de braille en italiano y estonio. Al restablecer las opciones predeterminadas de fábrica de NVDA, ahora hay disponible un botón «Deshacer» para recuperar la configuración anterior. Consulta todas las novedades aquí Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.2, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.2, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es f3f8d29974a88d687b3c4809be192219ec579c5bdabcda5aaf53635288bca824. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc2, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: In-Process 24th August 2026
en.summary: We’re so close to 2026.2 now! We have a release candidate! Plus, this time around: NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate! Automatically Scrolling the Braille Display Getting help from others New Unassigned Commands Finding out more about what is new NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate! The NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate is now available for testing! We encourage all… Read More
en.body:
We’re so close to 2026.2 now! We have a release candidate! Plus, this time around:

The NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate is now available for testing! We encourage all users to download this RC and provide feedback. Unless any critical bugs are found, this will be identical to the final 2026.2 release.

NVDA 2026.2 includes:

Magnifier (full screen, colour filtering, zoom, focus tracking) Improved touch gestures (links, form fields, etc) NVDA+x to repeat last spoken information Improved speech dictionaries Automatic Braille Display scrolling & much more!

We would encourage you to try out the NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate , especially if you haven’t yet tried any of the betas. You can do this by creating a portable copy or by selecting “Continue running” from the launcher, to run a temporary copy and not interfere with your installed copy of NVDA.

One of the new features in NVDA 2026.2, is that we: “Added the ability to automatically scroll the braille display”. This comes courtesy of Noelia, one of our prominent Spanish contributors. Reading the user guide entry for the new “Automatic scroll rate” feature, it notes:

Automatic braille scrolling can be enabled to scroll the display at a set speed. When using this feature, the braille display scrolls to present information which is more than will fit on the display at once. The feature is disabled by default. You can change the gestures assigned to use automatic braille scrolling in NVDA’s Input Gestures dialog before it can be used. Gestures are also available to speed up or slow down the rate of automatic scrolling. Alternatively, you can set the automatic scroll rate in Braille Settings.

While braille is scrolling, you can still use the scroll back and scroll forward commands without stopping scrolling. Scroll back can be useful to read previous contents again. Scroll forward can be useful to skip a blank line, or if the line being read is short.

While reading, automatic braille scrolling will stop when any of the following happen:

The toggle automatic braille scrolling key is pressed The user presses a key or gesture which would display a new message The focus is moved (including with braille display panning keys) The end of the document is reached The state of the lock or secure screen is changed (such as the computer being locked)

The commands for this feature are: Toggle automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+k Increase automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+L Decrease automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+j

Last fortnight, we covered ways you can get help from within NVDA itself. This time around, let’s have a look at some of the places you can get help from others. As with last fortnight’s post, this list covers getting help for NVDA itself only, aimed at end users: NV Access Telephone Support : If you’ve still got questions after following last fortnight’s tips and reading Basic Training for NVDA etc, give us a call. Telephone support IS a paid service, and for end-user support only, but it is available 24/7. We have numbers you can call in Australia or the USA, OR you can email us and we can call you anywhere in the world. You also get telephone support included with the NVDA Productivity Bundle . Official NVDA Email Group : While we monitor various other groups, the one place you know you will find NV Access staff, and users, is the official, friendly, NVDA email group at https://nvaccess.org/nvda-users – plus, as a free, welcoming and popular resource, you will often get help from other users even quicker than we can respond. Local language email groups : We have a huge list of email groups in many languages. Know of a group which isn’t listed? Please, let us know so we can share it on the connect page for others! Social media : Our community on Mastodon is the most active, but you can also find us on Facebook and other platforms . NVDA Remote Access : Have a friend who can help with your PC? You can let them connect to your PC to help you. Note there are a number of security measures in place to ensure this feature can only be accessed by deliberate action from both parties.

For the upcoming NVDA 2026.2, we’ve added a couple of new “unassigned” commands. These aren’t always the most obvious to find, so I thought it was worth highlighting them here: Added an unassigned command to toggle keyboard layout. ( #19211 , @CyrilleB79 ) Added an unassigned Quick Navigation Command for jumping to next/previous slider in browse mode. ( #17005 , @tareh7z ) Added an unassigned command to report the current status of the Screen Curtain. ( #19759 )

Commands like these can provide useful functionality, but may often only be required by some users. As we are all aware, screen readers already have a lot of keystrokes, so we always have to think carefully before assigning new keystrokes.

For instance, the toggle keyboard layout setting. Most users will setup the keyboard layout how they prefer, and never need to change it. For the rare time you may wish to change it, the setting is on the keyboard settings page, which is available with NVDA+control+k . For testing or teaching, a command to toggle the layout on the fly may be invaluable, so, in NVDA 2026.2, it’s there if you need it.

In any NVDA release announcement , there is a link to “ What’s new in this release of NVDA ” (I’ve linked to those to things for NVDA 2026.2 RC1). That document gives a summary of the highlights in several paragraphs, and then bullet points for all the changes in groups: Important notes : information such as older Windows versions no longer supported Security fixes : Updates to NVDA which fix potential security issues. New features : New functionality in NVDA. For instance, NVDA+x to repeat the last spoken information, or the ability to automatically scroll the braille display Changes : Features which may be slightly different, such as renaming the “COM Registration Fixing Tool” to “System Accessibility Repair Tool”. Bug fixes : Fixing features which didn’t work the way they should. For instance, in NVDA 2026.2, we’ve fixed a crash in the add-on store, NVDA now recovers quicker from freezes in some applications, and form controls are correctly reported in Firefox again. Changes for developers : Updates which may affect how contributors code for NVDA. These don’t affect end users directly. For instance, updating the version of Python used, or new functions developers can call to find out information. Deprecations : Again, only for developers, function calls which either no longer work, or have been changed to something else, and developers should transition over to the new function call.

In most of the bullet points for each release, there is a number at the end, and sometimes a username. For instance, in the unassigned commands article above: “Added an unassigned Quick Navigation Command for jumping to next/previous slider in browse mode. ( #17005 , @tareh7z )”

In this case, #17005 is the issue number assigned to the original request for this feature. @tareh7z is the GitHub user who wrote the code and submitted the pull request to fix it – thanks @tareh7z! And thanks to ALL our contributors. NVDA 2026.2 is a big release with a lot of amazing features the community have put a lot of work into!

The line in the changes document will hopefully give enough information to quickly describe the feature for most users. The user guide will also have been updated with any relevant information. In this case, look at section 6.1.3 “Other Navigation Commands”, which talks about not only sliders, but other quick navigation commands which don’t have default keystrokes.

The issue number is a link back to that issue, which can be helpful if you’d like to look back at the conversation which prompted the new feature. For instance, in this case, there was some discussion around what other types of information could potentially be accessed with a “slider” command (others that were suggested were ruled out in this case).

That’s all for this time. Do please try out the NVDA 2026.2 release candidate , and of course, let us know of any issues you encounter with it. Next time around we will have more on NVDA 2026.2!

en.title: A Comprehensive Guide to the Smart Typer Pro App
en.summary: Smart Typer Pro is an all-in-one productivity app for Android devices that completely redefines mobile note-taking, text editing, voice dictation, artificial intelligence assistance, and document…
en.body:
Published 15 August 2026 by Syed Sharib Ali

Smart Typer Pro is an all-in-one productivity app for Android devices that completely redefines mobile note-taking, text editing, voice dictation, artificial intelligence assistance, and document management. Rather than operating as a basic text editor or a single simple tool, Smart Typer Pro serves as a central, easy-to-use digital workspace designed for everyone—from everyday users, students, and writers to content creators and users who rely on accessibility features.

This comprehensive guide breaks down every single feature, setting, handy customization, system integration, and daily shortcut inside Smart Typer Pro in clear, easy-to-understand detail.

Download the app on Google Play

Table of Contents

Smart Typer Pro keeps all your work neat, organized, and easy to find on your Android phone or tablet. When you open the app, it automatically creates a main folder named Smart Typer directly in your device’s main internal storage root ( /sdcard/Smart Typer ).

Located at the bottom-right corner of the main screen, the Plus (+) / Create button lets you create new items instantly:

Located at the top-right of the main screen:

By default, long-pressing (holding down) any file or folder brings up a comprehensive context menu loaded with quick actions tailored specifically to the file type:

When you turn on multi-select mode (or select multi-file options), you can handle several items together:

The built-in editor screen is the heart of Smart Typer Pro. It handles everything from quick daily scratch notes to large document files smoothly.

Smart Typer Pro makes typing hands-free easy with voice dictation built straight into the text editor.

Set up custom shorthand phrases in Settings. For example:

While you speak, Smart Typer Pro automatically detects your custom shortcuts and expands them into full sentences instantly.

Smart Typer Pro offers four writing assistant options to refine your notes according to your needs:

The AI Typing Assistant screen offers a dedicated, distraction-free space for dictating text, polishing ideas with AI, and sharing messages directly.

Available from the main menu side drawer and directly from the text editor’s More Options menu, the Quick AI Assistant gives you a friendly, helpful AI chat companion ready to answer questions or help write content.

The Text-to-Handwriting feature turns your digital text notes into realistic handwritten PDF files or image pages.

Smart Typer Pro uses high-quality realistic voice technology to convert your text documents into clear, natural-sounding MP3 audio files. Conveniently access this feature directly from the long-press file context menu ( Convert to Audio ) as well as from the Smart Utilities Hub.

Smart Typer Pro includes built-in pop-up media players so you can listen to audio recordings or watch video clips without needing separate apps.

The Media Scanner tool quickly scans your phone to organize and show all your media files in one clean dashboard.

The Instant Translator tool offers fast, multi-language document translation. Access it conveniently from the Smart Utilities Hub , the long-press file context menu ( Translate Text ), or directly inside the text editor’s More Options menu while working on a note.

The Wikipedia Search tool lets you research topics and extract information right inside the app. Access it from the Smart Utilities Hub or directly while editing notes via the text editor’s More Options menu.

Word Helper uses AI to turn any word or phrase into a comprehensive, easy-to-understand dictionary guide. Access it from the Smart Utilities Hub or directly while writing notes via the text editor’s More Options menu.

The Smart Utilities Hub acts as a central control panel holding all 12 main tools of Smart Typer Pro (including Instant Language Translator, Wikipedia Search, Quick AI Assistant, Word Helper, and Text-to-Audio).

The Settings screen gives you full control over how Smart Typer Pro works:

Smart Typer Pro fits naturally into your daily Android phone routine.

Smart Typer Pro is set up to handle standard file actions across your system:

Disclaimer: This guide was provided by the Smart Typer Pro developers. It was not written or independently reviewed by the Accessible Android team.

Published in Tutorials

Published 14 August 2026 by Syed Sharib Ali

Smart Typer is a lightweight yet feature-rich Android productivity application designed to bring notes, file management, advanced text editing, AI tools, and everyday utilities into a single workspace. It allows users to create, edit, organize, copy, move, rename, share, and convert files while also providing an integrated file manager for browsing and managing device storage.

Its powerful text editor supports both regular writing and coding, with features such as Find & Replace, precise text splitting, multi-selection, voice typing, offline voice-input correction, Markdown/blog writing, and multiple AI-powered text refinement modes. Users can also translate text, look up words with Word Helper, search and read Wikipedia articles, and convert text into PDF, realistic handwriting, or natural-sounding audio.

Smart Typer also includes an AI Companion for answering questions with beautifully formatted responses, an AI Typing Assistant, Archive Viewer for ZIP/RAR files, image, audio, video, and Markdown viewers, and enhanced Microsoft Word document support. With extensive customization, tablet and landscape support, and compatibility with numerous text and document formats, Smart Typer aims to provide a versatile productivity environment for students, writers, developers, professionals, and everyday Android users.

en.title: Unboxr
en.summary: Unboxr is the ultimate lightweight and secure tool for extracting archives on your Android device. Designed with a beautiful, modern dark theme using Jetpack Compose,…
en.body:
Published 9 August 2026 by Warren Carr

Unboxr is the ultimate lightweight and secure tool for extracting archives on your Android device. Designed with a beautiful, modern dark theme using Jetpack Compose, Unboxr makes managing compressed files fast and intuitive.

Key Features:

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

“Unboxr” is a simplistic app intended for extracting compressed files, with support for several formats, including password-protected archives.

The UI is straightforward, with an “Open Folder” button that, when tapped, takes you to your phone’s internal storage, where you can choose the location containing the file you want to extract. The app also appears among the apps that can handle these file types, so you can select supported files from a file manager without using the dedicated button in the app.

In the top-right corner, there is a “Settings” button where you can customize the app. The customization options are quite limited, though. The Settings section also includes a donation option at the very bottom of the screen labeled “Buy me a coffee”

The app is completely free and contains no ads.

The app is very minimalistic. I noticed that it is not possible to make the app ask you where you want the contents to be saved every time you extract a file, despite the presence of an “Always ask” option in Settings, which, based on its explanation, should enable this behavior. Instead, to select the output directory, you have to specify it through the “Default destination folder” option.

When it comes to accessibility, I didn’t encounter any issues with the app.

v1.0. Android 16

en.title: In-Process 7th August 2026
en.summary: We’re getting ever closer to NVDA 2026.2 and we hit a new milestone towards that this week. Let’s have a look at what’s in this week’s blog and then dive in: NVDA 2026.2 Beta 10 Getting Help WebAIM Screen Reader User Survey Thanks Acapela Moving by Sentence NVDA 2026.2 Beta 10 NVDA 2026.2 is nearly… Read More
en.body:
We’re getting ever closer to NVDA 2026.2 and we hit a new milestone towards that this week. Let’s have a look at what’s in this week’s blog and then dive in:

NVDA 2026.2 is nearly here! This week we’re up to NVDA 2026.2 Beta 10 . We are now in the “String freeze” – that is, we don’t make any changes for a couple of weeks to give the translators time to update their work before the stable release. So, the next step should be a release candidate in a couple of weeks. Then, all going to plan, the final release a week or so after that. Let’s have a look at the updates from the betas since the last In-Process:

Changes introduced in NVDA 2026.2 Beta 10 : Updates to translations Fixed touchscreen, touchpad and mouse input for magnifier Added gestures for braille automatic scroll commands Removed True Center Mode and Border Mode from the magnifier due to design bugs Remove non-functional “Custom” option from the math decimal separator setting

Changes introduced in Beta 9: Updates to translations Update Braille Reading and Automatic Scroll Rate in User Guide Moving by sentence in Word (alt+downArrow/alt+upArrow) at the start/end of a document now stops there instead of wrapping around to the opposite end Changed quick access keys for magnifier settings to ensure they are unique Changes introduced in Beta 8: Updates to translations Improve magnifier behaviour when using higher DPI scaling Fix magnifier from interfering with opening dictionary dialogs Improve the handling of failing to activate the magnifier Block touch screen input when using the magnifier where possible, as it is not supported yet

We try to ensure there are plenty of ways for NVDA users to get help. Since you’re reading this blog post, I HOPE you would consider our blog one of the ways you learn more about NVDA. We have training material and telephone support in our shop, and they are both very popular options (particularly combined in the NVDA Productivity Bundle ). But what about in NVDA itself? There are a couple of ways you can get help while you are using NVDA: The User Guide. (And particularly the quick start guide for new users). The user guide contains information on all of the features of NVDA. It is an excellent resource to refer back to after completing “ Basic Training for NVDA ” and learning about all the features. Press NVDA+n to open the NVDA menu, then h for the help submenu, which starts on the User Guide The other items in the “Help” menu for information including what is new , links to the NV Access website , help and training , and the “ Commands quick reference ” (the tables of keystrokes and gestures extracted from the user guide). Context sensitive help. From within any dialog in NVDA, press f1 to open the user guide to the topic on the current control. Input Help. Press NVDA+1 (the 1 in the number row, above Q). In this mode, NVDA will report any key that you press. If you press an NVDA command (such as NVDA+tab), it will report that. Keys pressed and commands are not executed. This can be a great way of exploring a new keyboard layout. Press NVDA+1 again to turn input help off. Report keystroke: While we’re on help for individual keys, the Report Keystroke command tells you the keystroke to access the currently focussed control. Press shift+numpad 2 (laptop: NVDA+control+shift+dot ) to report the keystroke for the current control .

The WebAIM screen reader user’s survey is on again. This is the 11th edition of the survey, which is the largest survey we are aware of which collects data on screen reader usage and trends. We encourage everyone to complete it in order to give the community as accurate a picture of how you use a screen reader as possible!

The one question I’d like to highlight is “ Screen reader satisfaction ”. Please do answer all the questions honestly, including that one – but if there is anything which makes you think “I’m not 100% satisfied with NVDA” – please let us know! You can create an issue on GitHub (and we’ve previously included GitHub instructions here in In-Process , you can email us , reach us in the official NVDA mailing list , or on social media .

We are very grateful to all our donors . They are one of the main reasons we are able to continue to provide NVDA for free to anyone who can use it anywhere in the world.

This week, we’d like to give a shoutout to Acapela who make the popular Acapela TTS for NVDA . If you are interested in trying Acapela out, they offer an evaluation version which is fully functional and provides access to all voices and all functionalities for 15 days.

Acapela, along with many other options, are listed on our Extra Voices page .

And, if you would like to donate and help keep NVDA free for everyone, we would welcome your support. Please visit our donation page for PayPal or bank donation options. You can also become a GitHub Sponsor .

One of the fixes in the recent NVDA 2026.2 betas is a fix to moving by sentences in Microsoft Word. In many places in Microsoft Office, you can press alt+down arrow to move to the next sentence and alt+up arrow to move to the previous sentence. While this is a feature of Office, if you appreciate moving by sentence and would like to be able to use it everywhere, try out the “ Sentence Nav ” add-on in the add-on store.

Want more ways of getting around? How about: Word ( control+left arrow and control+right arrow ) Paragraph ( control+up arrow and control+down arrow OR shift+p and p ) And as an added bonus for paragraph navigation, here’s a related feature: Paragraph style , which lets you change how NVDA moves when moving by paragraph Single letter navigation What other ways do you prefer to navigate documents? Continue the conversation on social media .

That’s all for this week. Next time around we’ll be close to the final 2026.2 release, so for now, do try out the latest beta and be sure to report any issues. Also don’t forget to do the WebAIM Screen Reader User Survey .
